crucible5.subsystem: Crucible 5.0 experience interface (crucible.experience + crucible.rapid), the integration contract for CAM
crucible5.summary: The Crucible 5.0 learner interface is real and runs, but only partly. You call make(tier, name, seed, reward_mode) and get one ExperienceEnv (agents/observe/execute/observe_since/tools/advance/reward/verify) with one JSON Observation record. In this checkout only Tier 1 and Tier 0 build. Tier 1 is 25 4.0 mech families and 74 v5 rapid families (73 of them run). Tier 0 is 74 4.0 kernel world families, ow_* OpenWorld among them. Tier 2 is empty: the domain registry has nothing in it because I1-I4 were interrupted, and registry.py's Tier-2 code does not match the domains.base.Domain API anyway. Tier 3 is empty: crucible.civ has no generate. Measured speed: rapid median 3,600 steps/s (259 to 5,888); mech 2,400 to 4,600 decisions/s; OpenWorld ow_market 47.5 decisions/s with hourly decisions (2 sim-days/s) and 2.7/s with daily decisions; open_mixed 0.7 sim-days/s. Each kernel observation is 50 to 200 KB, mostly the repeated list of 145 to 230 tools. observation_only zeroes the reward everywhere. The leakage battery (11/11), the 4.0 byte-identity check (11/11 envs plus 4/4 kernel scenarios) and CAM's own 4.0-based env tests (20/20) all pass. Even so, I found real leaks the battery does not cover. (1) Every Mech-tier episode puts the task id 'family:seed' into the first observation's rig.episode event: 25 of 25 families, including all 11 test-split ones. (2) The rapid action query{target:'spec'} returns family, seed, split, engine, category and difficulty in 36 of 73 families. (3) In multi-agent rapid worlds, observe_since shows a third party the metadata of a private message between two other agents. RapidExperienceEnv, which came from the interrupted N2 merge, is broken for multi-agent worlds. Agents after the first get agent a0's result back: an invalid action comes back ok=True, {waited:true}. Joint 'coordinate' plans can never succeed, because each execute is a separate one-agent tick. Events are duplicated n_agents times and cursors don't line up. It also has no 'now', so FarmEnv crashes on rapid worlds. Its digest is not a state digest, and it reports world_changes=0. Verified labels are the weakest part. No released-label channel exists, only an env.verify() pull that mixes labels with private evaluator state. 0 of 74 rapid families define a success threshold, so verified_terminal_outcome pays nothing in Tier 1 rapid and outcome.success is always None. The kernel goal verifier gives false early success after a multi-day advance: one 3-day advance gives success at day 3 with streak 3, where hourly stepping gives day 5. Counterfactual forks are possible but not part of the interface. rapid/mech envs deepcopy in about 1 ms and replay deterministically. Kernel envs can't be deepcopied (thread lock); World.fork plus re-wrapping takes about 4 ms but drops the adapter's per-agent state. No CAM code imports crucible.experience. CAM's runtime.run_steps passes evaluator score increments to the learner as rewards (runtime.py:184-191), which is the opposite of observation_only. I wrote a scratch adapter against CAM's real interfaces.EnvAdapter: it runs on rapid, mech and kernel worlds, maps attribution correctly (delay_s/via/caused_by) and scrubs both identity leaks. So the design can carry the new observation-only, meta-learned-reward requirements once the defects below are fixed and the label channel, forks and held-out guard are built.

components.name: RapidExperienceEnv (adapter for v5 rapid worlds)
components.evidence: Merged from the interrupted ws-N2 (34e3f74, 808309b). Single-agent use works: median 3,600 steps/s. Six families are multi-agent (coop_split_info, team_assembly, team_commons, team_discovery, team_profile, team_schedule). rapid_coord2.py: a direct RapidEnv joint tick gives agreed=True, yield 69.33; through the adapter, a0 gets agreed=False and a1 gets {'waited':true}. An invalid a1 action returns ok=True {'waited':true}. rapid_multi.py: in team_commons, observe_since(a2,0) returns the a0->a1 private message event (to:a1), and tick events are duplicated 3x for 3 agents. With obs.cursor=5, observe_since still returns 10 later events. Two worlds driven with different actions have equal digest() while their outcome values differ. run_learner on rapid:hc_confounded reports world_changes=0 after 35 OK lever actions. t is the tick index, cost_s is always 0, advance ignores its seconds argument, and every event has cause=None, so rapid has no delayed provenance.
defects: crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:577 - uses out['result'] (agent a0's result) for every agent. Non-first agents get a0's result, so invalid actions are reported ok - high
crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:572-573 - one execute is one world tick with one agent, so joint plans (coordinate) are impossible and simultaneous play is serialised - high

crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:514-529,598-600 - one shared event log fed by every agent's observation. Events are duplicated n_agents times, private events of other agents reach observe_since, and obs.cursor (RapidEnv index) does not match observe_since seq - high
crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:620-621 - digest() = [name, seed, steps, cursors], not a state hash - medium
crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:572-596 - last_changed is never set, so run_learner world_changes is always 0 - low

crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:602-606 - advance(seconds) ignores the duration (at most one idle tick), and t/cost_s are in ticks, not seconds. This breaks the SMDP time contract that the other tiers follow - medium
crucible/src/crucible/experience/tier1.py:525 - cause is always None, so rapid never produces the delayed_consequences kind - low
actions: Rewrite around the RapidEnv joint step. Add execute_joint({agent: action}) -> {agent: result} built from out['results'][agent]. Keep execute(agent, a) as buffering, with the tick fired by advance(), so all agents' actions of a round share one tick.
Per-agent logs: call self.env.observe_since(agent, own_cursor) and keep one seq space per agent. Return obs.cursor in that space.
Declare tick_s (default 86400). advance(s) runs floor(s/tick_s) ticks (idle ticks when nothing is buffered). now = t*tick_s. result.cost_s = tick_s for an executed action.
digest = sha256 over engine.copy_state(self.env._state) plus ledger. Set last_changed when the engine state digest changes.
Attach cause={action_seq, tool, t, delay_s, via:'settings_in_force'} to tick reports produced under lever settings the agent chose (the same rule as Mech).

Tests: (a) team_discovery joint coordinate through ExperienceEnv gives agreed=True; (b) an invalid a1 action returns ok=False; (c) observe_since(a2) has no a0->a1 events; (d) no duplicate seq; (e) digests differ for different actions; (f) advance(3*tick_s) moves t by 3.

components.name: KernelExperienceEnv (Tier 0 / OpenWorld / future Tier 2-3 adapter)
components.evidence: 74 world families (train 24 / val 20 / test 28 / dev 2; ow_market, ow_frontier, ow_works, ow_composite, ow_heldout, open_* ...). Throughput (kernel_speed.py): ow_market at 1 h is 47.5 decisions/s (1.98 sim-days/s, 123 KB/obs, 204 tools); at 1 d it is 2.7/s (2.65 sim-days/s, 195 KB/obs, 94 events/obs). open_mixed at 1 d is 0.7/s (0.73 sim-days/s). ow_frontier at 1 h is 62.7/s. mech_scm_additive_tools at 1 h is 626/s. Goal-free by default: objective None, verify agents {}, reward 0. A cash GoalContract on ow_market (45 read-only tools called) shows no privileged keys and no family name; only verify() holds progress/streak/success_t. Lossless events, own-action causes and transaction caused_by all work (through my adapter). VERIFIER BUG (verifier_jump.py): a payer schedules a transfer landing at 2.8 d, and the goal is cash>=target sustained 3 checks. One advance(3 d) gives success_t=day 3, streak 3. Hourly stepping gives success_t=day 5, which is correct. deepcopy fails (TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread.lock'); World.fork plus re-wrapping takes 4.2 ms with the digest equal at the fork. It adds the 'exp' module by default, so the spec differs from the same 4.0 family.
defects: crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py:286-289 with goals/contracts.py:220 - advance() jumps the clock once, then RewardContract runs every missed daily check on the end state. Sustained goals succeed early, which corrupts verified labels exactly when CAM takes multi-day SMDP waits - high

crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py:151-165 - a single objective per agent (_objectives[agent]); there is no way to verify several CAM-generated goals - high (for autonomous goals and curriculum)

crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py:396-410 - verify() mixes authorised labels (success/failed/success_t) with private state (progress, streak, evaluator output); there is no release policy - high
crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py:250-258 - the tool cache is keyed on world.seq, so it is invalidated every step and 145-230 tools (50-125 KB) are re-serialised into every observation - low
crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py:76-78 - adds the 'exp' module unless experiments=False, so worlds are not byte-identical to the WorldServer worlds CAM uses today - low

crucible/src/crucible/experience/kernel.py (whole class) - no fork() keeping adapter state (cursors, objectives, cause map), no checkpoint/restore, no NPC participant scheduling. CAM's OpenWorldOperator has all of these - medium
actions: advance(): loop while target > now: nxt = min(target, min(next_check of each agent's verifier)); world.advance_time(nxt); self._tick(). Expose next_check from RewardContract (or keep a per-objective check clock in the adapter). Test: verifier_jump.py gives success_t = day 5 for both the 3-day jump and hourly steps.

Replace _objectives[agent] with dict[goal_id, verifier]: add_goal(agent, GoalContract) -> goal_id and remove_goal(goal_id). verify() returns per-goal status. Test: two goals on one agent resolve independently.

Add fork(): World.fork plus deep copies of _vis/_cause/_cursor/_artifacts/_objectives/gate. Test: drive a fork and the original with the same actions and the digests match; different actions give different digests.
Cache tools by content hash rather than world.seq.

components.name: Verified outcome label channel (trainer-only)
components.evidence: grep 'label' in experience/ finds only modes.terminal_labels(). The only path is env.verify() (pull, unfiltered). MASTER_SPEC 11.3 requires 'authorized verified outcome labels may be supplied separately'; that is not implemented. CAM runtime.run_steps computes rewards = new_scores - scores from GoalEvaluator.evaluate_goal and passes them to agent.observe (runtime.py:184-191), so evaluator progress currently reaches the learner directly. Label availability: kernel GoalContract gives success/failed/success_t; validated mech tasks give success at episode end; rapid gives a continuous value only, success None in 74/74 families.
defects: no released-label channel; the actor and the trainer can only both call verify() - high
superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/runtime.py:185,191 - evaluator score increments are fed as rewards to the actor/learner, which violates observation_only - high
actions: Implement OutcomeLabel {env_id, actor_id, goal_id, status in {pending, success, failure, uncertain}, t_outcome_days (success_t or the end time), t_release_days, value (objective quantity at resolution, e.g. rapid outcome.value, mech net_cents), verifier}. Build it with a LabelChannel(operator) that polls verify() after every advance, emits only status transitions, applies a release delay, and drops progress/streak/private keys. The trainer reads channel.take(); the actor process gets no handle.

In CAM runtime.run_steps, when reward_mode=='observation_only', pass rewards=[0.0]*B to agent.observe and route evaluator output to LabelChannel. Test: an actor-input hash (tokens) is identical with and without the evaluator; labels arrive only in the trainer store.

requirements.justification: The Crucible side exists: reward_mode='observation_only' in make() and all 4.0 envs, with 0 nonzero rewards in all probes. CAM has no reward_mode anywhere, no adapter imports crucible.experience, and runtime.run_steps feeds evaluator increments as rewards (runtime.py:184-191).

Shaped rewards are disabled and the battery passes 11/11, but there are measured leaks: the Mech task id 'family:seed' in 25/25 families (tier1.py:120); rapid query spec giving family/seed/split/engine in 36/73 (rapid/env.py:235); private message metadata reaching a third agent via observe_since (tier1.py:598-600). The battery has no rapid or identity coverage.

There are only two channels (observe vs verify). verify() mixes labels with private state, and there is no released-label channel (experience/ has no labels module). Rapid has no success labels (0/74 thresholds).

Kernel tier with objectives=None: objective None, verify agents {}, reward 0 (tiny, ow_tiny, ow_market, ow_frontier, open_mixed, mech_scm_additive_tools). Unvalidated Mech tasks also have no objective. Rapid families always carry a public objective text, which is not secret; the adapter can drop it. CAM has not run goal-free through it yet.

GoalVerifier has pending (success False, failed False until the horizon), success and failed, and never moves pending to failure before the horizon. There is no 'uncertain'. Measured: one 3-day advance() gives success_t at day 3 with streak 3, against day 5 with hourly steps (kernel.py:286-289 + contracts.py:220).
CAM has never run on KernelExperienceEnv. Mechanically possible: my scratch adapter drove ow_tiny and ow_market at 47.5 decisions/s (hourly) with 0 leaks and 0 reward.

crucible5.risks: 1) Label integrity. The kernel verifier gives false early success after multi-day advances (measured: day 3 instead of 5). Any CAM success/outcome predictor or meta-gradient outer loss trained on those labels learns from corrupted targets until kernel.py advance() is segmented at verifier check times. CAM's SMDP waits make this the common case, not an edge case. 2) Identity and held-out leakage. Task ids (25/25 Mech families) and rapid spec queries (36/73) reveal family, seed and split. A 1B-parameter core can memorise these, which inflates held-out results and makes the RUDDER/COCOA/curriculum (C_chi) evaluations invalid. Scrub in the CAM adapter now, and add identity-canary tests on both sides. 3) No success labels in the whole rapid tier (0/74 thresholds), and Tier 2/3 are absent. The goal-conditioned success predictors and the 'verified query performance' meta-objective therefore depend on evaluator-side thresholds that do not exist yet; until then use a continuous outcome value with an oracle-relative normalisation computed on the evaluator side. 4) Multi-agent rapid worlds (6 families) are unusable through RapidExperienceEnv: wrong results, no joint actions, private-event leaks. Any multi-agent or cooperation claim built on it is void until it is redesigned. 5) Throughput. The OpenWorld tier gives 2 to 2.6 sim-days per wall-second and 120 to 200 KB per observation. Lifetime-value or meta-learning experiments at main scale need many parallel worlds (FarmRun or CAM dist actors) and tool-list deduplication. Rapid and Mech tiers (2,400 to 5,900 steps/s) are where per-decision learning signal is cheap. 6) The 4.0 byte-identity proof loads only the top-level 4.0 module from c07098b against current dependencies, and the kernel scenarios use the deterministic cost model, so identity under the default cost model is not proven. 7) All 241 Crucible acceptance requirements and all CAM OB-* requirements are recorded as NOT_STARTED, and 13 of 24 Crucible workstreams were interrupted. Docstrings such as LEARNER_GUIDE section 2's 'No evaluator data ... (tested by Gate R)' overstate what the tests cover.

envs.subsystem: H-audit: Environments, OpenWorld adapter, Stage-1 runtime, agent loop, OW protocols (envs/*.py, envs/protocols/*.py, stage1/*.py, runtime.py, agent.py, integration_doubles.py; manifest ids A17 A18 A19 A22 G01-G09 W01 W05)
envs.summary: I ran real CAM decisions end to end: the real model, the real Qwen decoder and a real Crucible OpenWorld. Smoke 1 used the default dev configuration, with an 81.2M-parameter CAM (59.8M trainable) on Qwen3-0.6B in a process-isolated ow_tiny world. It made 9 decisions with 2 weight updates in about 880 s; my own 900 s timeout then killed it. Smoke 2 used a lean planner and made 12 decisions with 3 updates in 85.8 s. In both runs the mechanics work: decisions execute, outcomes are archived, the core weight hash changes, and the policy measured on fixed contexts changes afterwards. Tool-pointer entropy went 4.959 -> 4.426 -> 4.364 nats, and later decisions decoded fewer tokens (about 5,500 -> 1,900). The intelligence does not work yet. 0 of 21 actions were goal-directed. Arguments were fabricated, e.g. id.remove with invented ids or {"tool": "world.validate, args: { "}. 9 of 21 calls failed with not_found. Every reward was 0.0, so the actor objective collapsed into imitating its own choices (AWR weight about 1.0, advantage mean -2e-13), and the value head output stayed at 0 or about 3e-10 throughout. Throughput with the default planner is 23-247 s per decision (median 51 s); the GPU was shared with about 8 other jobs. The planner makes 104 Qwen action decodes per decision (model.py:1851). At that rate the 8-day open_economy episode needs about 1,100 decisions (about 15 h), and OW-1 needs about 12,500 decisions (about 7 days of wall time) at dev scale. There are two serious defects in the loop. First, the Stage-1 harness never puts a tool's result (documents, search results, error suggestions) into the next decision's input: 0 of 9 decision inputs contained a tool_result. Second, evaluator rewards (potential shaping on GoalVerifier progress plus a success bonus) flow into the agent's beliefs, its GAE targets, the world-model reward head and the planner's score. On leakage the adapter is good. The observation stream is byte-identical when only evaluator-side data change (150,629 bytes, canary absent), and no world family, seed or world id appears in it. However, nothing in cam_unified uses Crucible 5.0's reward_mode or observation_only mode (grep finds zero uses). There are four parallel decision loops with different reward and observation-merge rules: runtime.run_steps, envs.harness.run_lifetime, experiments.mechrun.run_batch and dist.actor._episode. All eight protocols (OW-1..OW-7 plus open_economy) are runnable, and their env tests pass (35 tests). There is still no CAM long-horizon run, and several predicates are missing. Recommendation: keep the adapter, firewall, protocols and record plumbing. Rebuild the evaluator into a reward-gated verified-label source. Make one canonical loop, derived from envs/harness.run_lifetime, used by every runner. Redesign the agent's reward and credit path around a CAM-internal reward R_psi. Move imagination out of Qwen decoding.

components.evidence: openworld_eval.py:55-87: the default objective is crucible.goals.contracts.RewardContract(task, shaping=1, bonus=1). Crucible's goals/contracts.py:216-229 gives r = shaping*(phi_t - phi_{t-1}) + a one-time success bonus, where phi = GoalVerifier.progress on the verified metric. components.name: Parallel decision loops (runtime.run_steps, experiments.mechrun.run_batch, dist.actor._episode, capabilities.loop.train_agent)
components.evidence: Call-site map (grep). runtime.run_steps is used by capabilities/* (train_agent with ScoreEvaluator) and semantic/demo_init. run_lifetime is used by stage1, protocols, demos, baselines and stage1/probes. mechrun.run_batch is used by experiments exp1, exp2 and train. dist.actor.Actor._episode is used by F2. Their semantics differ. Rewards: run_steps uses the difference of IndependentGoalResult.score, i.e. the evaluator's progress score (runtime.py:184). run_lifetime uses take_rewards (RewardContract). The dist actor uses take_rewards, falling back to score differences (actor.py:344-350). mechrun uses take_rewards or DelayedPartial. Next-observation construction: run_steps merges result, advance and collect_events by seq; run_lifetime uses advance only; mechrun concatenates result and advance without deduplication (mechrun.py:439); dist merges by seq. The same CamUnifiedAgent therefore receives different inputs and rewards depending on the runner.
defects: runtime.py:183-186 - reward = difference of evaluator progress score (evaluator-only state) - critical in observation-only
four loops with four observation-merge rules and three reward rules; capability results (Y), Part-17 experiments (X), Stage-1 (S) and distributed (F2) are not comparable - major

capabilities/envs.py:139-150 ScoreEvaluator: every diagnostic capability env is a payout-to-reward slot machine; none exposes payouts as observable consequences, so all capability tests assume extrinsic reward - major for observation-only
actions: Reduce run_steps, mechrun.run_batch and train_agent to about 10-line wrappers over the canonical run_lifetime, or delete them. The dist actor calls run_lifetime with sink=queue writer, learner=None and a weight-refresh hook at trajectory boundaries.
Diagnostic envs (capabilities/envs.py) emit the payout as an observable NUMERIC observation (e.g. balance) and use reward_mode, so the same tests run in observation_only.
Test: grep-based CI check that only cam_unified/runtime.py contains an act -> execute -> advance loop; a parity test that one scripted episode gives identical EventRecords through every wrapper.

components.name: CamUnifiedAgent reward / credit pathway (record plumbing is sound)
components.evidence: Reward path from code: agent.py:891,894 -> model.observe_outcomes -> tracker 'reward' spec (outcome_spec.py:135,219) -> beliefs/Kalman update, because reward_in_beliefs=True by default (model.py:823, 1279-1282). The evaluator reward therefore becomes part of actor-side state that conditions the next decision. The same reward feeds GAE (agent.py:252), the world-model 'reward' head loss (world/reward = 5.54 in update 1) and the planner's imagined return (model.py:1822). Measured with reward = 0 in smoke 1: policy adv_mean -1.96e-13 and return_mean 2.9e-10 in update 1; 3.6e-6 in update 2 (learning-progress term only). The AWR weight was 1.00, then 1.47, so actor = -logp of its own planner choice, i.e. self-imitation. Value-head output was 0.0 on all probe contexts at v0, v1 and v2, and about 3e-10 in smoke 2. Value gradient into the backbone was 0.0, 0.023 and 0.036. Probe tool entropy in smoke 2 drifted 4.959 -> 4.155 -> 4.507 -> 4.545, which is non-monotonic, as expected from noise-driven updates. Memory: 0 items retrieved in all 9 smoke-1 decisions. Reasoning ran 11-12 of 16 iterations.
defects: model.py:823 reward_in_beliefs=True + agent.py:894 - evaluator signal enters actor state (beliefs) - critical under strict actor/label/evaluator separation
agent.py:252 + 297 - policy/value targets are extrinsic reward + 0.1*LP; with zero reward the objective is behaviour cloning of the planner argmax and the value function is dead - critical

model.py:1822 - planner score = predicted extrinsic 'reward' channel + value; no goal-conditioned success/outcome/time/resource predictor, so in observation_only the planner has no goal-directed criterion - critical
EventRecord.reward (interfaces.py:237) conflates 'verified return' with whatever the learner trains on; no psi version / provenance - major
actions: Remove 'reward' from the actor-side realised outcomes (CORE_KEYS) and set reward_in_beliefs=False permanently. Beliefs condition only on observations.

Add an intrinsic reward head R_psi(Z_t, I_t, a_t, Z_{t+1}, G) owned by CAM. Archive EventRecord.extra['r_psi'] with its psi version, and keep verified labels in a separate LabelStore table keyed by (episode_id, goal_id).
Change gae_semi_markov to consume r = R_psi(...) (detached for the inner policy update). Add a lifetime value V_life plus RUDDER/COCOA terms in learn/ (owned by the learning auditor).

Make the planner score imagined trajectories with CAM's goal-conditioned success-probability, time-to-success and resource predictors plus V_life, all trained on LabelStore verified outcomes with calibration.

Tests: (a) in observation_only, act() inputs are identical whether the evaluator would have paid 0 or 1 (invariance). (b) The gradient of R_psi's loss reaches psi only through the meta path. (c) A planner-ranking probe on two candidate actions with known verified outcomes from the LabelStore ranks the successful one higher after training.

components.name: Stage-1 vertical path (runner, system assembly, HarnessAgent, tasks, probes, evidence, branch)
components.evidence: SMOKE 1: python -m superlearner.cam_unified.stage1 run --task open_economy --scale dev --sem-model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --update-every 4 --max-decisions 10 (default imagination: 8 candidates, horizon 4, 4 samples). The real stack was built in about 10 s with no doubles (system.py). CAM: 81.2M total / 59.8M trainable; core 14.5M; Qwen 600.6M with 4.59M trainable. The world was isolated (sqlite store). 9 decisions in about 880 s. act_s per decision: 33.2, 40.7, 36.0, 66.7, 70.3, 23.0, 51.2, 60.5, 247.0 (median 51.2). 104 actions were generated per decision, with 1,844-5,846 sampled tokens. 9/9 schema-valid and 8/9 ok, but 0/9 goal-directed. Tools: world.hosts, id.remove (fabricated ids, not_found), market.inventory x2, jobs.openings, cloud.deployments, world.validate (garbage args), world.whoami, mail.search (query echoing the bank summary). Updates took 13.1 s and 47.5 s and changed the core hash (c5db7670 -> b188b428). After the first update, per-decision tokens fell from about 5,500 to about 1,900. Version went 0 -> 3, and the core hash changed at every update. Earlier wave-2 evidence (S/explore1) was a 2-layer d64 configuration (5.1M parameters), 6 decisions, 5 of them not_found. requirements.justification: The real Crucible OpenWorld is used through the actor-only adapter, process-isolated, and my real-CAM smoke runs (9 + 12 decisions) went through it. test_openworld passes 14/14. The invariance and canary probe gives a byte-identical actor stream across evaluator-side changes. Open repairs: tool results never reach the next decision under the Stage-1 harness; there is no reward_mode or observation_only; provenance is direct-only; task and evaluator details reside in the learner process.

No CAM long-horizon run exists. The longest real CAM run is 12 decisions, about 0.1 simulated day; the earlier wave-2 runs had 6 decisions. Scripted 90- and 120-day runs exist. Throughput makes it currently infeasible: 23-247 s per decision with default imagination means about 15 h for the 8-day open_economy (1,101 decisions) and about 7 days for OW-1 (12,469 decisions).
Holdouts are defined and guarded (2/2 worldgen holdout tests pass; SplitGuard is enforced in stage1/tasks.py:47). Nothing has been evaluated on any holdout with CAM.

Real stack at dev scale with Qwen3-0.6B in a real isolated ow_tiny world: semantic observations -> CAM decision -> real execution -> archived outcome -> weight update (core hash c5db7670 -> b188b428; smoke 2 had three successive hash changes) -> the policy on fixed probe contexts changed (tool entropy 4.959 -> 4.426 -> 4.364) and later decisions decoded fewer tokens. It is not EMPIRICALLY_DEMONSTRATED. The only learning signal was the world model plus self-imitation (reward 0, value output 0), decisions were 0/21 goal-directed, and the main scale was not exercised.

test_sandbox_boundary_through_the_adapter passes. The OW-1 protocol opens and runs, and the 90-day Builder calibration reproduces in test_protocols. The $10k target is fair-feasible only at $3k (inductor, day 26). There is no recurring-revenue predicate and no CAM run.
OW-2 runs, and both controls succeed on day 3 of 30, so the threshold is too easy. There is no originality predicate and no CAM run.
OW-3 runs on engineering_lab. Only the privileged lab_greedy succeeds, and no non-privileged control exists. No CAM run.
The OW-4 RecoveryObjective works; the Builder record shows recovery on day 105. Only 3 shock kinds are supported, there is no fair control, no change-detection measure and no CAM run.
OW-5 opens and runs mechanically. There is no calibration record, and no industrial control (disclosed in ow5.py:61-65).
The OW-6 AntiTrivialFilter and SelfDirectedObjective pass their tests. The calibration record shows the task is infeasible (inductor fails). No CAM run.
OW-7 joint utility is now call-linked, and the tests pass. Calibration: relay day 12, shortcut and idle fail. The dependence audit checks availability, not content. No CAM run.

Fork-based calibration works and the records exist for 7 of 8 protocols. OW-5 has none, OW-6 is infeasible, and OW-3 and OW-4 have only privileged ceilings. Feasibility is therefore not established for the full set.
The holdout invariants pass and the 63-family validity record exists. The technical-failure dimension exists only in held-out families, and the mech worlds have the same extrinsic-reward dependence.
The shared-world heterogeneous population and the semi-Markov dt tests pass in my run, and the frozen-LLM participant test exists. Historical CAM checkpoints as participants are not exercised.

PROTOCOLS: envs/protocols/<owN>.PROTOCOL (TaskProtocol), plus ow1.OPEN_ECONOMY and ow1.open_economy_task(seed, days). TaskProtocol.open(split, i, isolated=True, evaluator={}) returns (adapter, op, ev); .calibrate(split, n_tasks, controls, days, think_s, record); .make_task(family, seed) attaches actor_handle and participant_factory. Custom metrics are registered in Crucible METRICS: cam_operating_profit, cam_operating_margin, cam_partner_payments, cam_joint_utility, cam_partner_dependence. CRUCIBLE 5.0 PIECES TO REUSE: crucible.experience.modes RewardGate(mode).add_legacy/verified/take, OBSERVATION_ONLY, VERIFIER_STATUS_KEYS, terminal_labels(); crucible.experience.leakage find_keys(x, PRIVILEGED_KEYS), canary_hits, new_canary; crucible/experience/kernel.py:168-200 `_scan` scheduled-cause tracking (sched.add -> proc job cause, via/delay_s). Spawned operator processes need an `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard in any script that calls open_world_isolated.
envs.risks: 1. My timings were measured on a GPU shared with about 8 other auditor jobs; the 247 s decision is probably mostly contention. Even so, the structural cost holds: 104 Qwen decodes per decision with the default planner, and the lean configuration is about 20x faster. All my runs used dev scale (8x384) with Qwen3-0.6B. The DOM target (1B core with 32 layers, Qwen3-4B with cross-attention into the decoder) was never run in OpenWorld, and it will be several times slower per decision. Imagination must move to the latent-intent space, or OpenWorld lifetimes stay infeasible. 2. Switching to observation_only removes every extrinsic signal. The policy and value currently degenerate to self-imitation even under legacy mode on ow_tiny, because early verified reward is 0. In observation_only, all goal-directed learning depends on the not-yet-existing R_psi meta-gradient, the verified-outcome predictors and the hindsight relabeling. Expect long stretches with no progress unless the curriculum starts from tasks that a non-privileged control reaches quickly (open_economy: inductor day 4). 3. In-world self-goal tools (goals.check_now/propose over independent_revenue) are an evaluator-grade oracle inside the world. The master must decide whether that counts as a legitimate observation; CAM already called goals.check_now unprompted. 4. Separation is process-level only for the worlds. The harness, the learner and the acting model share one process, and that process receives task definitions and evaluator details. A strict three-way split needs a separate harness/evaluator process or a hard API boundary, plus the reward-integrity tests listed above. 5. Several protocols lack fair feasibility (OW-3 and OW-4 only privileged ceilings, OW-5 no calibration, OW-6 infeasible, OW-2 trivially easy). CAM results on them would be uninterpretable until they are recalibrated. 6. The env-side unit tests (35 passed) exercise scripted policies. PolicyAgent receives results through observe_result, so these tests hide the CAM input-path defect (results not delivered). New parity tests must drive the CamUnifiedAgent itself. 7. Merged Crucible 5.0 is partly from interrupted workstreams (social, population, rapid). Reusing their modes and leakage helpers is low-risk; building new OW tasks on social/population worlds needs validity checks first.

research.summary: I read all five sources in full: Zheng et al. 2020 with its supplement and JAX pseudocode, RUDDER with its 93-page appendix, COCOA with appendices A-M plus its reference code, R-HCA (RLJ 2026) with appendices A-I plus its reference code, and HCA 2019. Nothing about R-HCA had to be guessed: the paper gives the estimator (Eq. 4), the algorithm, the network and the hyperparameters. The note is at /workspace/agentrs/superlearner/docs/CAM_UNIFIED_REWARD_CREDIT_RESEARCH.md. It is the only file I created in the repo; it is untracked and nothing was committed. I checked the core equations by exact enumeration. On a 128-trajectory noisy key-to-door, the estimators COCOA, R-HCA, HCA+, RUDDER with an exact decomposition, REINFORCE and Q-critic are unbiased to round-off (at most 6e-31). Return-conditioned HCA is biased (0.72 relative). HCA+ equals REINFORCE at the key decision (variance 11.054 for both). R-HCA's variance at the key decision stays at 0.411 whatever the immediate noise, while COCOA's rises from 0.411 to 2.312 to 12.293. RUDDER used as an immediate reward with an explaining-away decomposition has bias 1.00. The two published counterexamples reproduce exactly: R-HCA variance 400/9 against COCOA 326/9, and HCA-return advantages 1/3 and -4/3 instead of 1 and -2. Zheng's meta-gradient (Eq. 4) is exact only if the gradient is backpropagated through the whole lifetime (relative error 0.005, max z 1.1). Truncating to 1 or 2 inner updates gives relative errors of 0.60 and 0.30 while the cosine stays at 0.9999, so cosine-only tests cannot catch it. Several paper assumptions do not hold for CAM as published: finite enumerable actions, undiscounted absorbing episodes, rewards that arrive immediately and always resolve, a reward network that can see the extrinsic reward, on-policy hindsight models, and a Markov state (CAM's belief b_t encodes past actions, which makes state-conditioned HCA collapse to REINFORCE). The note specifies the adaptations: an estimator over the recorded candidate set, SMDP discount weights Γ, delayed and censored verified outcomes used as rewarding outcomes, reward-network inputs limited to what the actor observes, and a functional inner update on a small fast parameter subset. While I worked, the master committed tabular references (credit/exact.py, estimators.py, meta_exact.py, heads.py; commits 6b02749, e7f454b, d975c10). Their 13 tests pass. I found these problems: the function named hca_return_grad is actually COCOA's unbiased "Counterfactual Return", not Harutyunyan's HCA-return; R-HCA is missing; the sampled meta-gradient leaves out the score term for the inner-loop data, giving a measured bias at K=4 (relative error 0.015, max z 10.2, against 0.007 and 1.5 once the term is added); the hindsight model has no policy-logit input or policy-prior gate; and the return decomposer fits symlog targets with a Huber loss, so it does not predict the expected return. None of these modules is called by the runtime, so every component is IMPLEMENT and none counts as integrated.

components.name: Zheng et al. 2020 meta-learned intrinsic reward (lifetime meta-gradient, lifetime value)
components.evidence: Read paper and supplement (Eqs. 1-6, derivation in supp. A, Table 1 hyperparameters, inner_update/outer_update pseudocode). Exact diagnostic /tmp/claude-0/audit_research/scripts/metagrad_exact.py: 3-armed bandit, lifetime of 5 episodes, 3^5 x 2 histories enumerated. J=-0.7306, |grad|=0.7887, finite differences agree to 4.65e-11. Monte Carlo over 2e5 lifetimes: full backprop gives relative error 0.005 (max z 1.1); truncation to N=1 gives 0.597 (z 208) and N=2 gives 0.298 (z 65), with cosine 0.9999 in both; the episodic objective gives 0.021 (z 7.0); removing the pathway gives exactly 0. Audit of committed sampled_meta_gradient (audit_meta_sampled.py, 2000 repetitions, n_inner=64): K=4 relative error 0.015, max z 10.2; with the inner-data score term added, 0.007 and z 1.5. With n_inner=4: 0.022 (z 7.8) committed against 0.015 corrected. A grep shows credit/ and selfeval/ are not imported by agent.py, model.py or learn/*.
defects: superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/meta_exact.py:99-123 - sampled_meta_gradient differentiates only the query log-probs under theta_K and omits sum_{k>=1} grad_psi log pi_{theta_k(psi)}(b_k) * (J_query - c) (the inner data distribution depends on psi); measured bias at K=4 (rel.err 0.015, max|z| 10.2) - important
superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/meta_exact.py:113,120 - batch-mean baselines include the sample itself, which shrinks the inner and outer gradients by (1-1/N) (25% at N=4) - nit
superlearner/tests/cam_unified/credit/test_credit_meta_exact.py:30 - accepts cosine>0.95, which cannot detect a 60% magnitude error (truncated N=1 had cosine 0.9999) - important

superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/selfeval/intrinsic.py:1-25 - R_psi is normalised by running statistics of its own outputs; unless these are frozen inside a meta window, the reward being differentiated is not the reward the inner update used - important

superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/selfeval/intrinsic.py - R_psi is a per-transition function of (b_t, e_a, b_next) with no lifetime memory of its own; Zheng's ablation (Fig. 7) shows a feed-forward reward on the current step fails; e_a input may defeat transfer to new action interfaces (Zheng sec. 6.1) - important

superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/selfeval/intrinsic.py:134-135 - LifetimeValue uses symlog regression, which is biased as the bootstrap G^{life,phi} (needs the conditional mean in utility units) - nit
runtime - no differentiable inner update over CAM parameters exists; only the tabular reference - important
actions: Fix meta_exact.sampled_meta_gradient: keep theta_k with create_graph, accumulate inner_logp = sum_{k>=1} sum_i log pi_{theta_k}(b_k^i) and add inner_logp*(J_query - c) with c a constant or across-lifetime baseline (or switch to Zheng's formulation where rollouts 1..N are evaluated under theta_k with lifetime advantages). Use leave-one-out baselines. Test: exact_meta_gradient vs 2000-repetition mean at K in {1,2,4,8}, require relative error <0.02 and max|z|<4 per coordinate. Do not rely on cosine.

Port metagrad_exact.py into tests/cam_unified/credit/test_meta_lifetime_exact.py: lifetime of one-step episodes with stochastic inner updates, exact enumeration; assert the full-backprop Zheng estimator is unbiased (z<4) and truncation N=1 has relative error >0.3 (documents truncation bias); assert the episodic objective differs from the lifetime objective.

Define theta_fast explicitly (selection/evaluation head, r_psi value head, optional low-rank adapters on 2-4 late core layers) and implement the inner update functionally with torch.func.functional_call(create_graph=True) inside windows of K in {1,2,4,8}; theta_slow frozen in-window. Test: gradient into psi is non-zero; it is exactly zero when r_psi is detached in the inner loss; finite-difference directional derivative matches within 5% on a dev-scale CAM.

Outer loss per Zheng supp. C.2 adapted: -sum over rollouts 1..N and query of sg(A^ver) log sigma_{theta_k(psi)} + c_v*(V_L - G^{life,phi})^2 - c_H*H(sigma_{theta_k}), with A^ver from verified utility only and V_L bootstrap (Eq. 5). Psi is updated only by the meta optimiser; add a test that the actor optimiser's param groups exclude psi.

R_psi: freeze normalisation statistics within a window; give it a lifetime recurrent state (not reset at episode or objective boundaries); add an ablation without e_a. Integrity test: permuting or zeroing the label channel leaves R_psi outputs unchanged at fixed psi.

LifetimeValue: squared loss on linearly scaled verified remaining utility (or the mean of a distributional head); targets are n-step verified lifetime utility plus bootstrap; pending outcomes excluded until their window deadline.

components.evidence: Read HCA Thms 1-3, Eqs. 3-8, Algorithms 1-2 and App. E-F; COCOA App. K (HCA Thm 7 proof error) and App. L (HCA-return bias). The exact enumeration in credit_exact.py gives HCA-return relative bias 0.72 at sigma0=0.6 and 0.753 at sigma0=0 and 1.5. HCA+ t0-block variance is 11.054, identical to REINFORCE. components.name: RUDDER return decomposition and reward redistribution
components.evidence: Read RUDDER Thms 1-3, App. A2.6-A2.9 (Eqs. A113-A134), A4.1 tasks I-V, A4.2 (LSTM spec, lessons buffer, losses A268-A275, quality A267, PPO integration) and the github README. The exact enumeration (128 trajectories) shows: immediate redistributed reward with the exact g is unbiased, relative variance 2.077 against REINFORCE 36.424; with an explaining-away g, relative bias 1.00 (the key decision gets no credit); redistributed return-to-go is unbiased for any g but variance stays 35.4. Conservation held on every trajectory (<1e-12). The committed rudder_exact_redistribution and rudder_grad pass their MC tests (pytest: 13 passed).
defects: superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/heads.py:142,150 - ReturnDecomposer regresses symlog(G) with smooth-L1 and symexp's the output: not E[G|H_t], so the redistribution cannot be RUDDER-optimal (kappa != 0) even with infinite data; RUDDER's losses are squared - important

superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/heads.py:103-163 - only the L_c-equivalent loss; missing L_m emphasis, L_e (prediction of the prediction 10 steps ahead) and L_a auxiliary tasks, lessons buffer, quality measure and quality-gated advantage mixing - nit

superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/heads.py:112 - causal transformer replaces RUDDER's gate-less LSTM; RUDDER's argument against spurious contributions relies on predictions changing only when information is stored; unvalidated - nit
superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/credit/heads.py:158 - c_t = diff/gamma^tau is the correct discounted conservation, but 1/Gamma amplifies noise late in long lifetimes - nit
actions: Change ReturnDecomposer.loss to L = L_m + (L_c + L_e + L_a)/10 with squared error on linearly scaled G (RUDDER: r*10/g_max per objective family) or a distributional head whose mean is used. Test on NoisyKeyDoor-4 and Trace-Back: the trained F_xi gives conservation <1e-6 and a kappa-test E[sum future redistributed | s_t,a_t] within 0.05*|G| against DP.
Add exact kappa=0 test (note sec. 8.4) for rudder_exact_redistribution: by DP, the expected future redistributed reward given (s_t,a_t) is 0 for all t.

Add the discounted/variable-duration conservation test: random dt per decision, check sum_t Gamma_t c_t == G and that the redistributed return-to-go used in rudder_grad gives the exact discounted gradient in expectation.

Use redistributed rewards only for objectives whose utility exists solely at window end. Immediate-only credit requires the quality gate (a = a_o(1-q) + a_r q); otherwise use redistributed return-to-go. Add an accounting test that a verified utility unit is credited exactly once (CR-09).
Train F_xi only on resolved windows (resolved mask exists) from a lessons buffer prioritised by prediction error and return deviation (128-512 windows).

requirements.justification: credit/meta_exact.py has a differentiable tabular inner update (exact and sampled, create_graph). Nothing exists on real collected experience or on CAM parameters; selfeval/intrinsic.py is not called by the runtime.
A tabular query-surrogate meta-gradient exists, but it omits the inner-data score term, which I measured as biased at K=4 (rel.err 0.015, z 10.2). There is no CAM or Crucible implementation.
A LifetimeValue module exists (selfeval/intrinsic.py), trained with symlog regression. It is not used as a bootstrap or baseline anywhere and not integrated.

Committed tests cover exact-vs-finite-difference and the detach-gives-zero check. The exact-vs-truncated comparison is a cosine>0.95 test, which cannot detect the measured truncation errors of 0.30-0.60. My scratch exact test is not in the repo.

The exact tabular redistribution is tested (conservation). The learned ReturnDecomposer exists with discounted conservation but regresses symlog targets with Huber, so it is not a conditional-mean predictor, and it is untested and unintegrated.
Exact coefficients exist in exact.py. A learned HindsightModel pointer exists, but without the policy prior or time input, and it is not trained anywhere.

The tabular COCOA Eq. 4 is implemented (estimators.cocoa_grad) and passes MC unbiasedness and variance tests against exact gradients on key-to-door and a random tree (13 tests pass). My exact enumeration confirms the estimator mathematics. This is the reference only; there is no CAM extension.
An OutcomeEncoder module exists. It has no test of full predictiveness, approximation error or bias.
Candidate provenance is recorded (semantic/actions.py:787-797) and the hindsight model is a pointer over candidates. There is no candidate-set estimator and no coverage metric.
R-HCA is absent from the code. The paper, appendices and reference code are fully accessible, so this is not BLOCKED; the estimator and the tests are specified in the note sections 6 and 8.
No equal-budget comparison exists in the repo. My scratch exact table (note sec. 8.1) covers a single 4-step environment with ground-truth models only.
No credit estimator is wired into the learner; learn/ppo.py uses GAE on Trajectory.reward. The note sec. 9 gives a draft routing and accounting table.
No implemented loss/parameter/gradient-routing table or boundary gradient tests exist for these losses; only the draft table in the note.
No delay sweep at 16/64/256/1024 has been run. The exact DP testbed is specified in the note sec. 8.3.

A committed tabular test shows meta-training rewards the costly key pickup and beats training on the extrinsic reward (J 1.53 vs 1.12 per commit message). Nothing has been run at CAM scale or in OpenWorld.

research.interface_facts:
Notation: s~_t=(b_t,C_t); action j over the recorded candidates; sigma_theta(j|s~_t) is the selection policy; u = verified-outcome encoding; R = verified utility increment (never intrinsic); Gamma_{t,t+k} = exp(-kappa*(tau_{t+k}-tau_t)) (learn/returns.py:27).

COCOA (Meulemans 2023 Eq. 3-4): w(s,a,u) = sum_{k>=1} P(U_{t+k}=u|s,a) / sum_{k>=1} P(U_{t+k}=u|s) - 1 = h(a|s,u)/pi(a|s) - 1. Estimator: g = sum_t [grad log pi(A_t|S_t) R_t + sum_a grad pi(a|S_t) sum_{k>=1} w(S_t,a,U_{t+k}) R_{t+k}]. Unbiased iff U is fully predictive, i.e. P(R_k=r|S_0,A_0,U_k=u) = P(R=r|U=u). Sampled alternatives (Eq. 27): (1/M) sum_m grad log pi(a_m|S_t) sum_k w R, with a_m ~ pi drawn independently of A_t. Discounted (App. J): w_gamma uses gamma^k sums; hindsight CE weighted by gamma^k (use Gamma_{t,t+k} for SMDP). Hindsight model h(a|s,u,logits): CE over pairs (t, k>t); feed policy logits (Prop. 5). Contrastive alternative: w = exp(logit_D) - 1.

R-HCA (Ramesh 2026 Eq. 4): g = sum_t sum_a grad pi(a|S_t) sum_{k>=0} (h_k(a|S_t,R_{t+k})/pi(a|S_t)) gamma^k R_{t+k}; actor loss -sum_i sum_a pi(a|S_i) sg(G(i,a)); h trained by CE on all pairs (i, j>=i) including (i,i); ratio clamp 10; compute ratios before updating h on the same batch. Contextual bandit: Var(COCOA) = Var(R-HCA) + E[Var(COCOA|S,R)]. General MDPs: Var(COCOA_t) - Var(R-HCA_t) = [Var I_COCOA - Var I_RHCA] + 2 Cov(D_t, G_fut,t); counterexample 400/9 > 326/9.

HCA (Harutyunyan 2019): A(x,a) = r(x,a) - r_pi(x) + E[sum_{k>=1} (h_beta(a|x,X_k)/pi - 1) gamma^k R_k]. Return-HCA: grad log pi(A_t)(1 - pi(A_t)/h_z(A_t|X_t,Z_t)) Z_t, biased unless h_z>0 for all reachable z. The unbiased counterfactual-return form is sum_a grad pi(a)(h_z/pi - 1) Z_t.

RUDDER: optimal redistribution E[R_{t+1}|s_{t-1},a_{t-1},s_t,a_t] = q(s_t,a_t) - q(s_{t-1},a_{t-1}); contributions h_0 = g(D_0:0), h_t = g(D_0:t) - g(D_0:t-1), compensation R_{T+2} = G - sum h_t. Loss L = L_m + (L_c + L_e + L_a)/10 (squared errors, so g is a conditional mean). Quality = 1 - |g - g_hat_T|/mu/(1-eps); a = a_o(1-q) + a_r q. Discounted conservation: c_t = [F(H<=t) - F(H<t)]/Gamma_t plus offset and residual, giving sum_t Gamma_t c_t = G. Immediate-only use is unbiased only for the exact g; redistributed return-to-go is unbiased for any g.

Zheng 2020: J(eta) = E_{theta_0,T} E_tau[G^life]. Inner: theta_k = theta_{k-1} + alpha grad J_eta (actor-critic on r_eta, episodic gamma_bar=0.9). Outer: grad_eta J = E[G^life_t grad_theta log pi_{theta_t}(a_t|s_t) d theta_t/d eta], exact only with d theta_t/d eta through the whole lifetime. Truncation N=5 with G^{life,phi}_t = sum_{k<n} gamma^k r + gamma^n V_phi(tau_{t+n}); V_phi trained by TD on extrinsic lifetime return. Rollouts 1..N are evaluated under theta_k(eta) with stop-gradient lifetime advantages; outer entropy term; 64 lifetimes/batch; Adam 1e-3; gamma 0.99; r_eta and V_phi are LSTMs over the lifetime with arctan output. In CAM: inputs must be actor-visible only; labels enter only via the outer loss and V_L targets.

Existing code entry points: credit/exact.py (TabularMDP, key_to_door, random_tree, exact_gradient, q_values, future_outcome_counts, contribution_coefficients, hindsight_action_probs, sample -> Batch(s,a,u,r,logp_b)); credit/estimators.py (reinforce_grad, all_actions_grad, cocoa_grad(theta,batch,w[T,S,A,U]), hca_return_grad [mislabelled], rudder_grad(immediate_only), rudder_exact_redistribution, estimator_stats); credit/meta_exact.py (inner_updates_exact, exact_meta_gradient, sampled_meta_gradient [missing inner score term], finite_difference, meta_train); credit/heads.py (OutcomeEncoder, HindsightModel.logits(b_t,u,e_g,cand,cand_mask), contribution_coefficients(h_logits,logp_policy,cand_mask,clip=10), ReturnDecomposer.redistribute(x,mask,G,e_g,t_days,gamma_tau)); selfeval/intrinsic.py (IntrinsicReward, ExperienceSignals, LifetimeValue); semantic/actions.py:775-797 (sample_candidates, select_candidate storing proposal {n, probs, chosen, proposal_logp}); learn/trajectory.py Trajectory(reward, dt, done, behavior_logp, model_version, ..., extras); learn/ppo.py ActorCriticObjective (GAE/V-trace, max_policy_lag).
research.risks: 1) Hindsight models are policy-dependent and trained on-policy in every paper. CAM's distributed learner has policy lag, and no paper validates an off-policy correction, so this must be measured (note sec. 8.6). 2) The candidate-set estimators are exact only for the selector's gradient given the proposed candidates. They assign no credit to actions that were never proposed, and the proposal gradient I derived is unverified at scale, so candidate coverage can silently limit learning. 3) Delayed or pending verified outcomes: excluding pending outcomes biases credit toward outcomes that resolve quickly unless credit waits for window deadlines. 4) R-HCA itself reports that hindsight methods trail actor-critic when feedback is dense and informative, or when the reward is multi-factor (Lunar Lander). The default estimator must come from Exp. C, not from preference. 5) Second-order meta-gradients through the 1B core are infeasible, so the design depends on a small fast parameter subset; meta-learned reward quality is bounded by what that subset can express, and truncation bias is large (0.30-0.60 relative error on the exact problem). 6) Under observation-only operation the reward network cannot see outcomes as Zheng's does, so results like Random ABC may not transfer. 7) The scratch scripts in /tmp/claude-0/audit_research are not durable; the tests in note sec. 8 must be ported into tests/cam_unified/credit/. 8) The master was committing to this branch while I audited; my code notes reflect HEAD 3e53fba (commits 6b02749, e7f454b, d975c10). 9) The note is the only file I created and it is untracked; nothing was committed.

beliefs.subsystem: Fast adaptation, particles, Bayesian last layer (core/beliefs.py, core/bayes.py, outcome_spec.py channels/reward, model.py observe_outcomes / filter_sequence / adapt_loss, agent.objective_adapt, capabilities/beliefs.py; manifest A05, A06, D06)
beliefs.summary:
The pieces are numerically sound in isolation, but their composition fails. The particle belief does not work in the integrated agent. BayesLastLayer's float64 Joseph/NIG recursion is exact: it matches closed-form BLR to 1.7e-11 (fixed noise) and 2.4e-11 (NIG) after 5000 near-collinear updates, and P stays PSD. When I train the real BeliefModule and the real OutcomeHead on their own with a consistent likelihood and the support/query loss, they reach near-oracle on simple mechanism worlds: Gaussian query NLL 0.942 -> 0.046 against oracle 0.722 -> 0.031, cover90 0.91-0.94; Bernoulli 0.730 -> 0.514 against 0.693 -> 0.501. That is on par with an amortized GRU baseline (0.696 -> 0.523). The runtime composition breaks this. A single per-key Kalman residual layer sits on top of the particle mixture, its predictive variance replaces the mixture's, and it fits the residuals of the mixture mean. This removes all learning signal from the particles: with Kalman on, particle spread is 0.004 (0.98 without), the mixture NLL is flat at 1.45 for every k, and zeroing the proposal changes nothing. The combined predictive is also badly underconfident (z-sd 0.32-0.64) and 0.15-0.85 nats worse than particles alone. Adding a particle-only auxiliary loss revives the particles (mixture NLL 0.049 at k=16), but the Kalman-replaced predictive that decide() reports is then 0.349, about 7x worse in nats. This reproduces the wave-2 integrated evidence: a particle effect of -0.02 against a Kalman effect of +-0.96, particle spread 0.007 against a mechanism gap of 2.0, Bernoulli P(ok) stuck at 0.478 for both p=0.2 and p=0.8, and an integrated predictive std 3-5x too wide (derived NLL 1.46 -> 0.68 against an optimum of 0.033).

Other defects:
- The particle weights use a separate act_cond likelihood instead of the world-model prior Z_hat that decisions use.
- With the default zero FiLM init, act_cond gets about 3e-7 gradient.
- The misspecification test and the learning-progress signal look only at the particle mixture and ignore the Kalman layer.
- Expansion in particle space does not restore calibration (unfamiliar mechanism: cover90 0.011 after expansions). Particles alone become falsely certain: NLL goes 28 -> 58 after one observation.
- The Kalman layer has no forgetting (after a switch, |err| is still 1.0 500 steps later) and is never inflated on an alarm.
- Kalman state never reaches belief tokens, so policy, value and VOI are blind to the only adaptation that works.
- The verifier-computed reward is always fed in as an observed belief outcome, which breaks the observation-only separation.
- In adapt_loss, query states come from the full filter. The leak is structural, |dZ| 4.8e-7 at init.
- adapt_loss draws one k per update, does not handle episode boundaries, and real paths train only k <= 16 (stage1) or k <= 4 (capabilities).
- The correct, tested SupportQueryLoss in learn/meta.py is not wired into the runtime.
- Hypothesis x action interaction mechanisms are not learned by either particles or the GRU baseline through OutcomeHead FiLM: NLL flat at 0.693 against oracle 0.497.

Verdicts: keep the Kalman numerics. Redesign the particle+Kalman composition as a Rao-Blackwellised particle filter, with per-particle conditional Kalman statistics, which spec 5.1 already lists. Repair the belief-module likelihood, initialisation and misspecification, and the runtime and adapt-loss plumbing. Extend the Kalman layer and the evaluation harness. Implement differentiable belief-change and information-gain features for the meta-reward work.

actions: Replace the composition with a Rao-Blackwellised particle filter (spec 5.1 lists 'conditional fast adaptation statistics'). Give FastState per-particle Kalman statistics bayes_mu [B,K,C,F], bayes_P [B,K,C,F,F] (or a shared P with per-particle mu when the noise is shared), with phi_k = Phi(feat, particle k). The weight update uses the per-particle Student-t predictive of the residual y - mean_k; the predictive is the K-mixture of (mean_k + phi_k^T mu_k, Student-t scale_k). Memory at K=16, C=35, F=16 is ~2.3 MB per env.

Cheap interim if the RBPF slips: keep a shared Kalman layer but (a) compute the combined predictive as a precision-weighted fusion or a learned gate g(n, surprise) between the mixture and the Kalman predictive, instead of replacing the variance; (b) always add the particle-only query term (-mixture_ll on all outcomes) to adapt_loss; (c) randomly disable the Kalman layer for 50% of adapt_loss calls.

components.name: Differentiable belief-change / information-gain / posterior-sampling features for meta-learned rewards and VOI
components.evidence: Neither module has an API that returns belief change. The only belief-change signal is 'lp' in observe_outcomes (no_grad, particle-only, model.py:1496-1500). BeliefModule.update and BayesLastLayer.update are differentiable inside filter_sequence/adapt_loss: torch.where, gather and closed-form Kalman, with only resampling indices and alarm decisions discrete. grad_paths.py confirmed finite gradients into belief and Bayes parameters from the world loss through filter_sequence. Data-dependent Python control flow (bool(x.any()) at core/beliefs.py:452,474,497 and core/bayes.py:228,241) works with torch.func.grad but blocks vmap. Belief tokens lack Kalman state, so VOI(a) = E_y[max Q(b_updated)] - max Q(b) computed through the value head cannot see the Kalman adaptation.
defects: missing API - no differentiable info-gain features (KL(w_t||w_{t-1}), entropy drop, Kalman 0.5*(logdet P_{t-1} - logdet P_t), predictive-entropy reduction on probe queries) for R_psi, curriculum or VOI - important
missing API - no posterior-sample operator (Thompson: one particle, w_c ~ N(mu, P)) for the posterior-sampling baseline the meta-reward spec requires (section 8.2) - important
actions: Add model.belief_change(fast_prev, fast_new, probe_ob=None) -> dict of [B] tensors {kl_weights, d_entropy, kalman_ig = sum_c 0.5*(logdet P_prev - logdet P_new), probe_lp_gain}, differentiable when called inside filter_sequence. Record a no_grad copy in EventRecord.extra['belief_change'].

Add FastState.sample_hypothesis(generator) -> FastState (one-hot logw on a sampled particle; bayes_mu ~ N(mu, P) with P -> 0) and model.voi(state, candidates, n_y) using cloned updates (the planner already clones FastState).

Tests: kalman_ig equals the analytic Gaussian information gain on a 1-D example; gradient of kl_weights wrt BeliefModule.prop parameters is non-zero after one support step; sample_hypothesis leaves the original FastState bit-identical.

requirements.justification: The Kalman/NIG recursion is exact (closed form to 2e-11 over 5000 near-collinear updates, PSD). In the real integrated stack (Y evidence beliefs_s0/s1) a trained agent's predicted reward moves 0 -> +-0.96 after 7 pulls (abs_err 1.0 -> 0.08), caused by the fast state. However: (1) the effect is almost entirely the per-key bias feature (a running residual mean); (2) the predictive is 3-5x too wide (z-sd 0.21-0.36, pred_var 0.55 against 0.0625), and the derived NLL at k=7 is 0.68 against an optimum of 0.033; (3) non-continuous outcomes are not adapted at all (Bernoulli NLL flat at 0.667-0.722 against 0.500); (4) there is no forgetting, so drift is not tracked (|err| 1.0 500 steps after a switch); (5) the layer is not conditioned on hypotheses (d_cond unused); (6) the Kalman state is invisible to policy and value. Held-out NLL and calibration were never measured by the harness.

The mechanics (importance weighting, systematic resampling, ESS rejuvenation, CUSUM ARL) are correct, but they were tested only with an exact DoubleOutcomeHead. In the real integrated stack the particles do not represent competing hypotheses: prediction spread 0.007 against mechanism gap 2.0, particle-mixture effect -0.02, mass_on_active for 'high' 0.34 -> 0.006, no Bernoulli adaptation; the learned test is xfail. My module experiments isolate the causes. The shared residual Kalman layer kills particle learning (spread 0.004 against 0.98 without it; proposal ablation a no-op). The zero-init FiLM leaves act_cond with ~3e-7 gradient. Hypothesis x action interactions are not learned (NLL 0.693 against oracle 0.497). Misspecification alarms fire late (k>=8) and expansion leaves cover90 at 0.011. Particles alone become falsely certain on an unfamiliar mechanism (NLL 28 -> 58).

The runtime objective (model.adapt_loss via agent.objective_adapt and dist/cam_learner) exists and backpropagates through the differentiable particle and Kalman updates; gradients reach the belief, Bayes, outcome-head and core parameters. It violates strict separation: query states are filtered Zs[t] that depend on earlier query outcomes (structural, measured |dZ| 4.8e-7 at init). It has no episode-boundary reset and one k per update, and the real paths train only k<=16 (stage1) or k<=4 (capabilities). The separation-correct SupportQueryLoss in learn/meta.py, which the D06 evidence describes, is not wired into any runtime path, and the integration test of adapt_loss uses DoubleBeliefs/DoubleBayes.

At init, gradients from L_world (through filter_sequence belief tokens) and L_adapt reach beliefs.prop/tok_*/prior_* and bayes.* (bayes only from adapt). Two exceptions: beliefs.act_cond gets 3.9e-9/3.3e-7 at the default film_init 0, and beliefs.ev_* get 0 at init (zero-init proposal output). No gradient reaches the beliefs from the policy or value losses except through the token encoders (policy_evaluate uses a stored detached FastState).
There are no differentiable belief-change or information-gain features, no posterior-sampling operator, and no VOI over belief updates. Learning progress is particle-only and no_grad.

From code: outcome_spec.py:219 marks the reward observed unconditionally and reward_in_beliefs defaults to True. In observation_only runs the beliefs therefore ingest reward=0.0 every step (runtime.py:188), and with an evaluator the private evaluator score enters the actor's FastState.

beliefs.risks:
1. RBPF memory and compute at the main scale. Per-particle Kalman statistics at K=16, C=35, F=32 are ~4.6 MB per env in float64, so either reduce F to 16 or share P across particles. The particle-conditioned outcome head with d_model=1536 over B*K*Q tokens costs about 1 TFLOP per call and is invoked in decide, observe (x3), every filter step and every adapt step: budget it, or evaluate particles on a reduced query subset.
2. The hypothesis x action failure also affects an amortized GRU baseline through the same OutcomeHead FiLM. Fixing the belief module alone will not deliver A06 on interaction mechanisms; workstream C's conditioning pathway must change, and the experiment must be repeated in the integrated stack, where belief tokens also reach the core and WM prior. My module experiments lack that path.
3. All module-level conclusions come from a 64-wide config, 1000 Adam steps and one seed per condition. The integrated numbers are derived from recorded wave-2 Y JSONs (batch-averaged mean/var, approximate NLL), not re-run: the GPU lock queue blocked my integrated rerun. Main-scale behaviour (d_particle 256, 32-layer core) is unverified.
4. Removing the reward from belief outcomes in observation_only mode removes the one channel through which A05 currently 'works' in MechanismEnv. Expect A05 capability numbers to drop until CAM-generated targets or observation-derived numeric outcomes replace it; this is correct behaviour, not a regression.
5. Forgetting factors and alarm-coupled covariance inflation interact with the CUSUM false-alarm calibration. Re-validate ARL0 (target 1e5) after the change.
6. Fast state persists across weight updates within an episode (stale feature basis). Long OpenWorld lifetimes amplify this; re-filtering costs extra compute per agent.update.
7. Data-dependent Python control flow in update() blocks torch.vmap for meta-gradient inner loops (torch.func.grad works).

semantic.subsystem: Semantic encoder, tokenizer, bridge, action decoder, grammar/constraints, objectives, sandbox, demo-init, dist/semserve (workstream A/A2; manifest A02 A10 S01-S04 D04; DOM-03/04/09/10)
semantic.summary: The mechanics mostly work. Calls are schema-valid by construction: 80 of 80 probe actions on 10 real ow_tiny tools were valid. Behaviour log-probabilities are exact: the recorded value equals the recompute and a permuted-subset recompute bit for bit. Gradients reach R, the bridge and LoRA. KV-cached decoding and the encoder hidden-state cache are sound. The semantic intelligence does not work. (1) Today CAM conditions Qwen only through a 16-vector soft prefix at the input embeddings (bridge.py, grammar.py:1336-1362). The prefix base is initialised from the embeddings of the literal phrase " Plan, evidence and intent from the controller:", and that text leaks into generated strings. (2) A token-boundary bug in the JSON string constraint (constraints.py:93: a closing quote is allowed only as a token's last character) forbids the tokens Qwen actually uses to close a string ('",', '"}'), which hold 51-99% of its probability mass. The constrained probability of closing drops to 4e-5..0.22. This is the root cause of the wave-1 strings of 1,536 tokens and more. A2's LengthHead only truncates them: max string now 196-576 tokens, but 41 of 80 probe actions end a string with a stray comma, 24 of 80 contain digit runs of 12+ digits, and 5 contain JSON fragments inside strings. (3) The CAM tool pointer is a bilinear pointer over pooled embeddings and does not generalise semantically. My rerun of S04-1 gave held-out 0.016 against chance 0.2, control 0.23 and train fit 0.94. The recorded S04-3 run equals its control (0.45 = 0.45) and S04-7 has a flip rate of 0.0. (4) Demo-init reached 8% non-wait tool accuracy, although the demonstrator's 25-step script is identical in every episode: a position predictor scores 100/100 and a bigram 96/100. Causes: homogeneous wait/act batches; joint gradient clipping while bridge gradients are 130-5,300 against 1-40 for the core, which scales act updates by 1.7e-4..6e-4; a loss dominated by string tokens; no backpropagation through time (BPTT) through Z. The checkpoint prefers wait at 75% of non-wait decisions. (5) There is no action intent I_t and no CAM evaluation of the concrete action before execution in the default path. The planner path evaluates candidates but decodes with Qwen at every imagined step and has no exact selection probability. (6) The semantic objectives are not wired into the integrated learner, and the masked objective test now fails (acc 0.13). The DOM hardware target is feasible: Qwen3-4B frozen (7.5 GB, decode 41-49 ms/step) plus a 0.91B core (32x1536) trained end to end through 6 gated cross-attention layers and a prefix needs 2.6 s per step at B=4 with a 24.3 GB peak. Gradient norms reach the early/middle/late core layers (21.2 / 3.9 / 2.7). Gated cross-attention by wrapping or hooking Qwen3DecoderLayer is compatible with KV-cache generation (fp32 difference 6e-5..8e-5) and with frozen-Qwen gradients, including gradient checkpointing. The newly committed decoder_xattn.py (DOM-03) is not wired in, and its alpha=0.05 initialisation changes 17-24% of top-1 tokens on JSON text, contrary to its docstring. Bottom line: keep the exact-logp / replay / grammar-walk / encoder-cache machinery. Fix the string constraint and the gradient scaling. Replace prefix-only conditioning with gated multilayer cross-attention driven by an explicit intent I_t. Build the intent -> generation -> evaluation bottleneck (DOM-04), which does not exist.

components.name: LatentBridge soft prefix P_t=W(R,G,B)
components.evidence: This is the only latent conditioning of Qwen today: 16 RMS-normalised vectors spliced into inputs_embeds after '<|im_start|>assistant\n' (grammar.py:1336-1362). Two random R differ by 19% in prefix norm; the same action's token logp under R1 vs R2: -8.67 vs -9.57 (decoder_probe). In 2 of 80 probe actions the generated text copies the prefix-init phrase ('Plan and Evidence and Intent from the Controller'). Per-sample BC gradient in the integrated dev model (Qwen3-0.6B, held-out demo steps): bridge 132-5,345 (out.weight dominates) vs core 1.0-40 and LoRA 6-2,103. The global norm of 145-5,746 gives a clip scale of 1.7e-4..6.9e-3 on string-bearing actions (bc_gradsplit.json).
defects: bridge.py:64 / actions.py:147 - the prefix base is initialised from token embeddings of the phrase ' Plan, evidence and intent from the controller:', which the LM reads as text and copies into arguments - important
bridge.py:59-61 - output renormalised to the embedding RMS behind Qwen's input RMSNorm (~1/0.03 amplification). out.weight gradients are 10^2-10^3 x the core's - important
Prefix only: no conditioning at decoder depth, so the decoder can ignore CAM after a few layers. DOM (A) requires multilayer gated cross-attention - important
actions: Make the multilayer gated cross-attention (decoder_xattn, repaired as below) the primary CAM->decoder path, conditioned on [R; I_t; G; B-summary] tokens. Keep at most a small optional prefix.

If the prefix is kept: initialise the base to zeros (or the mean embedding row) plus a zero-initialised residual with a learned gain, with no RMS renormalisation. Test: no init-phrase substrings in 200 sampled strings; bridge/core gradient-norm ratio < 10 on a BC batch.

In learn/trainer.py:289 and demo_init.py:588, clip gradients per optimiser group (core / heads / semantic) instead of one global norm. Test: core update magnitude on string-bearing batches within 3x of string-free batches.

components.name: decoder_xattn.LatentDecoderConditioning (DOM Mechanism A, commit b9162eb made during this audit)
components.evidence: My check (Qwen3-0.6B fp32, JSON-argument text, random Z, committed defaults alpha_init=0.05, d_attn=256). Every 4th layer (7 layers): top-1 agreement with the unconditioned decoder 0.76-0.83, mean KL 0.22-0.40 nats/token. Every 2nd layer (14 layers): agreement 0.68-0.79, KL 0.50-0.71. KV-cache vs full forward: 8.4e-5 max logit difference. Gradient checkpointing, with the condition() context closed before backward: gradient relative error 0.0 (the hooks are checkpoint-safe). My own wrapper prototype with a zero-initialised gate: output bit-identical at init (0.0 diff); alpha still gets gradient (0.0139) while z grad is 0; once open, gradients reach z (7.8e-3) and adapters with 0 Qwen params receiving gradients; decode overhead +2% (B8, 0.6B, 4 layers), +12% (B8, 4B, 6 layers: 40.6->45.6 ms). Not wired: config dec_xattn_every=0 and no caller in actions.py, grammar.py or encoder.py.
defects: decoder_xattn.py:56,81 - alpha_init=0.05 with injection scaled by rms(H): Qwen hidden states have huge outlier dimensions, so 5% of the inflated RMS spread over all dimensions perturbs the ordinary dimensions strongly. At init it flips 17-32% of the argmax tokens on JSON text, contradicting the docstring and the manifest claim 'preserves the pretrained argmax' - important
decoder_xattn.py - not attached by QwenSemantic and not used by HoleFiller._sample/score. Manifest DOM-03 says IMPLEMENTED while its own limitation says 'Not yet wired' - important
test_dom_decoder_xattn.py - the preservation test uses one prompt and TV<0.5. There is no exact KV-vs-full equivalence test and no checkpointed-backward test - nit
actions: Set alpha_init=0.0 (tanh'(0)=1, so the gate still learns) or zero-initialise self.o. Replace 'rms(H) * unit(a)' with a plain residual 'tanh(alpha) * a' from a zero/small-initialised o, or scale by a robust statistic (median |H|) that excludes outlier dimensions. Test: logits bit-identical to the unconditioned model at init; top-1 agreement >= 0.99 at alpha=0.05.

Wire it: in HoleFiller._sample and score (grammar.py:1373, 1459), wrap enc.step/decoder_hidden in enc.conditioning.condition(Zc[rows]) with rows aligned to hole_rows (actions.py:452) and per row in exact_rows scoring. Test: rescored logp == recomputed logp bit for bit with conditioning on; after 100 BC steps, ablating Z changes token logp by > 1 nat/action.

components.name: ActionGenerator (tool pointer, evidence pointer, typed heads, exact log_prob, provenance D04)
components.evidence: Exactness: recorded logp [-77.80, -11.67, -79.96] == recompute == permuted-subset recompute, bit for bit; the incremental path drifts 0.015-0.36 nats (diagnostic only). 80/80 probe actions schema-valid. Gradients to R: evidence 0.018, heads 0.021, tokens 0.297. OpenWorld acting (evaluation.json, 1.7B): executed_ok 30% (init) / 37% (BC). Demo-init BC checkpoint on held-out episode 100500: mean log p(demo tool) at non-wait decisions -3.63 (uniform over ~147 tools is -4.99), log p(wait) -1.46; wait is more likely at 75% of non-wait decisions. Default decision path model.py:1362-1366: sample -> executed. The world-model prior and value (model.py:1384-1388) are computed after selection and never gate execution. Planner path (model.py:1771, 1851) runs full Qwen decoding for every candidate and every imagined step; logp is the proposal logp; the argmax selection has no probability. Options (learn/heads.py:202, 16 discrete 'latent intents') only enter goal_in. They are not a per-decision intent that conditions generation and is evaluated.
defects: actions.py:286-506 - no action intent I_t. The decision is tool pointer -> evidence -> typed heads -> strings with no latent intent that conditions generation and is scored before execution (DOM-04) - important
model.py:1362-1366 - the default path executes the decoder sample without any CAM evaluation of the concrete action - important
actions.py:324-326 - the bilinear tool pointer over pooled TOOL tokens plus a context-free tool_prior. S04-1 held-out 0.016 < chance 0.2; BC tool logp near uniform - important
model.py:1851 - imagination calls ag.sample (Qwen decoding) at every imagined step for B*n*ns rows; intractable at 4B - important

actions.py:418 vs 451-459 - all structure (array lengths, optional keys, union members) is fixed by typed heads before Qwen writes any string. The LM then writes JSON keys and values inside strings (probe: 'to': ['bakery-07], ', 'subject', ...]) - important

actions.py:260-273 - the decoder prompt has no goal text and no history. Evidence candidates are only the current step's observations, but 276/476 demonstrated string arguments are ids from earlier observations - important
actions: Implement IntentHead: I_t = K latent tokens (e.g. 4 x d_model) sampled from a parametric distribution over [R; G; B; M] with exact log-prob. The tool pointer query, evidence pointer, typed heads, LengthHead and decoder cross-attention are all conditioned on I_t. Record I_t and its log-prob in the decode record.

Implement ActionEvaluator: encode each concrete candidate (tokenizer.action) -> world_model.prior + outcome head + value -> Q(s, a). Generate K candidates conditioned on I_t and select with a tempered softmax over Q, so behaviour logp = log p(I_t) + log p(a_k | I_t) + log softmax_k(Q/tau), exactly recomputable. A veto or 'regenerate' option precedes execution. Route every executed action through it (runtime/agent assertion).
Move imagination to the intent/action-token level (the world model consumes I_t or ACTION tokens) instead of decoding strings per imagined step.

Add an LM compatibility feature for tool choice: decoder log p(tool name | prompt, I_t) under a trie constraint over available names, computed under CAM conditioning and used as an input to CAM's pointer logits (CAM still decides; log it).

Extend evidence candidates to a CAM-managed working set: entity registry strings and retrieved archive artifacts across history. Add a string-span copy head for identifiers (as numsrc does for numbers).

Tests: zeroing I_t changes the tool/argument distribution; the evaluator rejects a candidate whose predicted outcome is a known failure; the selection probability is included and replays bit-exactly; no runtime path executes an action whose record lacks an evaluator stamp; S04-1 held_out >= 0.45.

components.name: Schema-walking grammar, HoleFiller, LengthHead and JSON/regex token constraints
components.evidence: quote_boundary.py (Qwen3-0.6B fp32, natural JSON argument prefixes). Probability on close-and-continue tokens such as '",' '"}' '"],': 0.99 / 0.94 / 0.51 / 0.97. Lone '"': 1.2e-6 / 9.8e-6 / 1.9e-5 / 7.3e-3. Constrained p(close) after renormalisation: 1.0e-4 / 1.7e-4 / 3.8e-5 / 0.22. decoder_probe (default options, 10 ow_tiny tools x 8 samples): action tokens mean 26-216, max 275; per-string max 196; 41/80 actions have a comma right before the forced closing quote; 24/80 have 12+ digit runs (e.g. handle 'b2b-07-089999999999999999999999'); 5/80 have escaped JSON fragments in strings. Recorded A2 benchmark at 1.7B: without the length prior max 1,606 tokens; with it max 217-576. code.run demonstration arguments are unrepresentable: '.input: value matches no member of the type list' (untyped_depth=2).
defects: constraints.py:93 (simulate_json_string) - 'return (k == last), True, ...' forbids every token that closes the string and continues the JSON. Qwen's natural closing mass is removed, strings almost never end on the LM's own choice, and generation drifts until the LengthHead/cap stops it (root cause of the degenerate strings) - important

grammar.py:1060-1121 LengthHead - hides the boundary bug with an artificial stop hazard. Its contribution enters every string's exact logp (BC must learn L_c/w_c instead of the LM closing) - important
grammar.py:76,590 untyped_depth=2 - nested untyped values (code.run input) cannot be represented, so the revenue-critical demonstrated call is excluded from BC (17 train / 4 held cases) - important

grammar.py:1243-1262 - per-hole caps are schema-derived but the action budget max_action_tokens=3072 equals 2*max_arg_tokens. The demonstrated code.commit service.py (2,375 chars) sits near the limit - nit
actions: Boundary-aware closing: precompute for each token the suffix after its first unescaped quote. At a hole allow token t if suffix(t) is a prefix of the next forced segment's text (forced[k+1] decoded). On such a token, advance the forced cursor by len(suffix) characters and re-tokenise the remaining forced text. Store the consumed count in the decode record so score() replays it exactly. Apply the same to pattern holes and keys.
After the fix, recalibrate the LengthHead (or start it with a ceiling near 0 for short/text classes) and measure natural closure.
Raise untyped_depth to >= 4 and add a generic 'JSON value' hole (Qwen-written JSON under a JSON grammar) for deep untyped leaves.

Tests: on 50 ow_tiny string slots with Qwen3-0.6B greedy and no length prior, >= 90% of strings close by the LM's own choice and none end with a trailing ','; records containing merged close tokens replay bit-exactly (rescored == recomputed); demonstrated code.run arguments are representable; 145/145 ow_tiny tools remain schema-valid.
