components.name: Demo-init behaviour cloning on ExampleInductor transcripts
components.evidence: evaluation.json: held tool_acc 0.43 overall, non-wait 8/96 = 0.083; exact args non-wait 0.083; greedy tools wait 130/156 (only 60 of 156 are waits); logp_act -167.7 -> -12.8; acting non-wait ok 20.8% (BC) vs 30% (init). The ExampleInductor's non-wait sequence is identical across all 16 ow_tiny episodes: position predictor 100/100 held-out, previous-non-wait bigram 96/100, previous-tool bigram including waits 68% on non-wait. BC checkpoint diagnosis: per-part held-out non-wait logp tool -3.63 / evidence -0.81 / heads -0.21 / tokens -7.37. For use.report steps after waits: log p(wait) about -0.004, demonstrated tool about -5.6 (uniform). Gradient split at init: on string-bearing actions the global norm is 145-5,746 (bridge-dominated), so the update is scaled by 1.7e-4..6.9e-3; on string-free actions the norm is 30-63 (scale 0.016-0.033).
defects: demo_init.py:607 - data.sort(key=is_wait) builds pure-wait and pure-act batches. Under the joint clip, wait batches get ~10-100x larger effective steps, so the policy learns 'wait' - important
demo_init.py:588 - one global clip_grad_norm over core+heads+bridge+LoRA. Bridge gradients of 10^2-10^3 starve the tool pointer and core - important
demo_init.py:584 - loss = -(tool+evidence+heads+tokens), unweighted. String tokens (-150..-1,851 nats/action at init) dominate the tool term (~-5) - important
demo_init.py:334 - StepInputs store state.Z.detach() and BC recomputes one step. No BPTT, so the script phase and timers (when to report) cannot be learned into Z - important
demo_init.py:426-428 / runtime merge - obs_lists hold only the current step's observations. 276/476 demonstrated string arguments are ids seen earlier and invisible to the decoder - important
actions: Shuffle waits and acts within batches (remove the sort) and use per-group clipping. Normalise string-token loss per token (or weight parts) and report per-part held-out metrics.
Train on sequences: truncated BPTT over K=16-32 consecutive decisions through Z (and beliefs), not single detached steps.
Run >= 5k updates; record a no-demo arm; add evidence candidates from a working set or memory (see ActionGenerator).
Test: held-out non-wait greedy tool accuracy >= 0.9 at dev scale (the bigram reaches 0.96) and exact-args >= 0.6; acting non-wait ok rate rises above the init arm's 30%.

components.name: Shared semantic server
components.evidence: The CAM actor policy builds its own full model and Qwen per actor process (dist/cam_policy.py:84-98, DIST_DEFAULTS: Qwen3-0.6B, max_arg_tokens=32). semserve.generate (semserve.py:239-293) is unconstrained HF generate with prefix only (no grammar, no cross-attention). Its 'hidden' op defaults to the final layer (-1), while QwenSemantic uses layer 0.75 with standardisation, so representations differ between paths. At 4B each per-actor copy costs 7.5 GB, so the learner (24.3 GB measured) plus at most ~2 actors fit on 48 GB.
defects: semserve.py:94-135 - not used by the CAM decoder. Per-actor Qwen copies do not scale to 4B - important
semserve.py:239-293 - generate op lacks the schema/grammar constraints and CAM conditioning, so it cannot serve CAM actions with exact logp - important
semserve.py:95 hidden_layer=-1 vs encoder.py layer=0.75 - inconsistent semantic features - nit
actions: Turn semserve into the single shared constrained decoder and encoder. Op 'decode_action' takes (ctx ids, hole programs or templates, conditioning tensors [R;I_t;G;B], temperature, seed) and returns hole tokens plus learner-path logp parts. Op 'hidden' uses QwenSemantic's layer and standardisation. Conditioning and LoRA weights are versioned like the adapter.
Test: actor logp via semserve == learner recompute to < 1e-3 nats; 8 actors sharing one 4B copy with peak memory < 40 GB including the learner.

decoder_xattn.py (committed during the audit) works with the KV cache (8.4e-5) and passes gradients under checkpointing. But it is not wired into the action generator (its own limitation says so; default dec_xattn_every=0), and its alpha=0.05 init flips 17-32% of top-1 tokens on JSON text, contradicting the 'preserves pretrained' claim.
There is no I_t and no pre-execution evaluation in the default path (model.py:1362-1366). Planner evaluation exists but decodes at every imagined step and has no selection probability.

Generation probabilities are recorded exactly (bit-exact rescoring) and candidate/proposal provenance exists. Generator-vs-selector learning is not distinguished or measured, and planner selection is a deterministic argmax.

Only fixed rank-16 LoRA on decoder q,k,v,o and a frozen encoder exist (reusable infrastructure: merged acting, versioning). There is no progressive unfreezing schedule and no retention evaluation of language/code competence.

semantic.risks:
1. The token-boundary fix changes the decode record format (consumed forced characters). Bump DECODE_VERSION and refuse old records. Existing demo/replay logp values become incomparable.
2. Cold start: neither the prefix nor cross-attention conditioning carries goal semantics until trained, and the decoder prompt has no goal or history text. Unless CAM can point evidence at goal and history text, early RL strings stay generic. Pretraining the conditioning with BC or grounding objectives (after fixing the clipping) is needed before RL.
3. Gradient scale: semantic-side gradients through Qwen's input or hidden scale are 10^2-10^3 x the core's. With a 1B core and 4B decoder, any shared global clip silently freezes the core. Per-group clipping or normalisation is mandatory.
4. Throughput: eager 4B decode is 41-49 ms/step and rescoring adds a teacher-forced forward per action. Imagination that decodes strings at every imagined step is infeasible. Plan intent-level imagination and static-cache/graph decoding.
5. Memory: the E2E learner step uses 24.3 GB (B=4). Merged-LoRA acting adds ~1.9 GB at 4B, and each per-actor 4B copy adds 7.5 GB. Distributed acting needs a shared server (semserve redesign).
6. S04 evidence is at tiny core scale. A larger core plus DOM-05 S_t cross-attention may change the outcome, but the bilinear tool pointer's memorisation failure is architectural and should be re-measured after the redesign at dev and superlearner scale.
7. The master architect committed during this audit (b9162eb decoder_xattn, bb5ef16 DOM-05 and the 1B scale, 4168579). My findings cover HEAD at audit start plus decoder_xattn.py. core/semantic_xattn.py was only checked for its S_t interface.
8. Several small Qwen3-0.6B probes (each under 4 GB) ran without the GPU lock. All 1.7B/4B, S04-rerun and decoder_xattn checks ran under it. GPU numbers come from a shared GPU (±15% timing noise).

h.summary: None of the four foundational experiments has been run on CAM. Nothing has a confirmation result, and no trained CAM checkpoint has ever been evaluated. Workstream X built a sound, leakage-safe harness for Experiments 1-3: identical support, queries forked on the evaluator side, proper scoring, a two-level bootstrap, and SplitGuard-checked seed ranges. It pre-registered U-X1..U-X3 (commit 4fe037d, 08:54, before any confirm-set evaluation). Only baselines were run on the dev sets: NIG exact/meta, GRU/attention predictors, Crucible model_based/ppo_gru/probe/random/hold, and KG/Thompson/greedy/random. The only CAM row in any experiment is an untrained dev-scale model on Exp1 condition A, seed 0. Its decision regret stays flat (familiar 0.329→0.355 over k=0..64) while nig_meta's falls (0.240→0.058). CAM was trained at dev scale (8x384, 81.2M params, Qwen3-0.6B, fixed J=4) for 3 seeds x ~10k decisions. Its checkpoints CANNOT be loaded by HEAD: CheckpointMismatch on 11 missing action_generator.length_head.* keys added later by the A2 merge. So every Exp1/2/3 CAM condition is currently blocked. I forced a non-strict load. Trained seed 0 then scored 0.016 on 8 familiar dev tasks (always 'set', 0/8 successes). Untrained scored -0.135, hold -0.022, model_based 0.536. Its prediction regret is identical to untrained to 4 decimals at k=1,2,4,8. That points to flat, action-insensitive reward predictions, which matches Y's integrated finding that per-action prediction differences are only 0.0085. Exp3 target runs, Exp4, the frozen-semantic/CAM-6.1/CAM-7.0 baselines and the CAM ablations were never run (CAM 7.0: seed 0 trained only, never evaluated). Every CAM experiment path feeds the environment's verified reward into the agent. That violates the new observation-only default, so the drivers need redesign around R_psi and must be re-run at the DOM architecture. The dashboard does render real traces, but the only CAM traces anywhere are 6-8 decisions from S's OpenWorld smoke run, and the experiments attach no TraceRecorder. test_manifest.py checks structure only. The new verify_completion.py is a reasonable skeleton but is gameable: I showed it reports X01 as EMPIRICALLY_DEMONSTRATED with verdict 'NOT_DEMONSTRATED', a governance test as the integration test, a test function as integration_entry and verified_by='anyone'. Evidence integrity is otherwise good. Y recorded its negative results honestly as xfail, and the 54 hashed X/Y run files match BACKUP_SHA256. model_based decision rows reproduce exactly (max diff 0.0), but only with the trained checkpoint, whose path is not recorded anywhere.

h.risks:
1. Compute: dev-scale CAM training cost ~50 GPU-span minutes per 10k decisions per seed, with 17-19 GB peak per process; three parallel runs plus cam7 OOMed the 48 GB card. The DOM main configuration (~1B core + Qwen3-4B with multilayer decoder cross-attention) will be roughly 10x slower per decision. The full Exp1-3 protocol (3+ seeds x 5 transfer conditions x confirm sets) is not feasible at main scale before the rental ends (2026-11-30 03:00 UTC). Plan dev-shape controlled experiments plus a single-seed main-scale demonstration, and report it as such.
2. The existing CAM training produced no measurable benefit. Trained decisions score 0.016 vs hold -0.022, with the policy collapsed to 'set'. Prediction regret is unchanged and consistent with action-insensitive predictions, and the integrated causal action-difference is 0.0085. The experiments will likely return FAILED_EMPIRICALLY until the core/world-model/credit redesign lands. That is an honest outcome, but don't spend confirm sets on models that have not passed dev.
3. All 12 X checkpoints are unusable under HEAD without a migration. Any further merge that adds a module will silently invalidate checkpoints again unless an arch hash and an explicit migration are added.
4. With 3 seeds the pre-registered two-level CIs under-cover (~0.78), so a 'demonstrated' claim could be a false positive. Fix the statistics before any confirmation.
5. The pre-registrations U-X1..U-X3 describe the old reward-supervised, dev-scale design. Changing to observation-only and the DOM architecture requires new pre-registrations (U-X1b...) committed before any confirm evaluation. Confirm-set supports already sit on disk (exp1/exp3 confirm pickles), so keep them untouched.
6. verify_completion is currently gameable (verdict substring, free-text verified_by, doubles in integration tests). If it is not hardened first, later agents can report completion falsely.
7. Shared GPU lock contention: about 7 waiters were queued during this audit. Experiment jobs must be chunked to <=10-15 min holds and resumable.

archive.subsystem: Archive, retrieval, replay, consolidation, checkpoints, plasticity (workstream E: superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/memory/*, experiments/exp3.py; spec Parts 10, 11; manifest A11 A12 A13 A14 A15 A21 E01-E05)
archive.summary: The storage layer works. The learning layer of memory does not exist in the real runtime. The Parquet+SQLite EventArchive has no lifetime ingestion cutoff. My measurements: 200k events at 5.8k ev/s and 392 B/event; reopen in 0.32 s with an exact count; SIGKILL lost 0 of 15,000 acknowledged events; StorageLimitExceeded is raised explicitly with du at or below the budget. The MemoryIndex, ArtifactStore and version partitioning are sound, and migration semantics are now correct. In the real Stage-1 stack (Qwen3-0.6B plus every real component, ow_tiny OpenWorld, 12 decisions and 4 updates, run twice), three things are missing. (1) The retrieval query net never trains: L2 change 0.0 and no gradient hook ever fired. (2) The memory objective sends zero gradient into the core (backbone grad norm 'memory' = 0.0 at every update). (3) Memory values reach the core without a gradient (stored_memory_tokens is @no_grad, and Retriever has no memory_tokens). The compression loss stayed at chance (2.21 vs 2.08). Memory tokens changed Z by only 0.3-0.6%. Wave-2's delayed-cue run through the complete architecture is consistent with this: retrieval hit-rate 0.0 after training and accuracy 0.0 in every condition. I read those result files; I did not reproduce them. Several costs grow with the lifetime and act as hidden lifetime cutoffs. (a) _memory_sync re-encodes the whole index synchronously inside update() every 4 updates: 278 s for 202k events, which projects to about 23 min per 1M events. (b) Parametric-provenance linking writes about 88k rows (10 MB) per update with 1,024 retrieved segments, which exhausts the default 200 GiB budget after about 20k updates. (c) Every checkpoint copies the whole memory index. (d) update_log grows without bound. Three gaps block the requested extensions. There is no store for delayed-outcome links or labels: attributed_to is neither indexed nor filterable, and records are immutable apart from fixed tags. The memory event encoder reads the evaluator reward (it changes the event token by L2 4.79), which is an integrity leak. Plasticity instruments find 0 of the core's 8 SwiGLU layers and are not wired into training; exp3 never got past 'prepare'. On weights-only checkpoints: the file itself is clean. But load_weights_only on a used agent leaks the fresh on-policy buffer, loss_mag, trainer n_updates/stage, outcome trackers, option, last_actions/last_now and the RNG. All seven checkpoint operations exist, but every one of their tests runs on a ToyAgent double. Recommendation: RETAIN archive, index and artifacts (with extensions). REDESIGN retrieval, migration and memory-to-core coupling. IMPLEMENT the outcome ledger, the link index, the latent cache, label separation and plasticity integration.

components.name: Retriever (learned query, segment encoders, memory tokens into the core)
components.evidence: p3_runtime.py, real stack (Qwen3-0.6B, every real component, ow_tiny open_economy, 12 decisions, 4 updates, memory_sync_every=1), run twice (max_ctx_tokens 64 and 384). Per-group retriever parameter L2 change: query_net 0.0, long_encoder 0.0, log_tau 0.0, segment_encoder 2.29/2.37, event_encoder 0.18/0.21. Gradient hooks fired only on segment_encoder and event_encoder and never on query_net. Backbone grad norm of the 'memory' objective was 0.0 in all 4 updates (learner/updates.jsonl), so memory never shapes the core. Compression loss was 1.81, 2.25, 2.25, 2.21 against chance 1.79, 2.08, 2.08, 2.08. Memory tokens in replay: 4-16 per step, relative dZ with vs without them 0.0054-0.0064 (0.0032-0.0039 in devctx). MEMORY tokens dropped by fit_budget: 0 of 24 decisions, but those runs had at most 6 segments. p1: the untrained query maps 16 random Z to only 5 distinct top-1 segments out of 7,200 (hubness). At DOM width 1536 the retriever has 170.6M parameters: 77.2M online encoders, 77.2M frozen target copies and 16.2M query net. Wave-2 Y delayed-cue run through the complete architecture (runs/cam_unified/wave2/Y/exp/memory_*_s0.json, real components on CPU, 360 updates; I read it but did not reproduce it): 'memory' hit rate 0.047 -> 0.000 among 1,824 segments; accuracy 0.0 in the ablated, memory and memory_episode conditions, against chance 0.25, even with the cue in context 100% of the time; retriever_has_loss=false and retriever_has_memory_tokens=false.
defects: retrieval.py:359 idx.search(v, q.detach()) plus model.py:1308 @torch.no_grad decide: no gradient path to query_net at all. Query never trained in runtime - critical

model.py:194-196 KIND_PRIORITY gives MEMORY the lowest priority (3), below ENTITY/RELATION (4) and observations (5). At the default budget (384 = 192 obs + up to 128 entities + 256 relations + B/G/TIME) entity-rich steps drop memory first - major (structural)

featurize.py default event encoder: semantics-free, hashes only the first 48 words per observation (featurize.py:83), and reads evaluator reward/cost/done (featurize.py:163) - see the HashedEventEncoder component
actions: (1) Move memory out of the fit_budget context into a dedicated gated stream inside CAM layers, the same mechanism as DOM (C): Z_{l+1} = Z_l + F(Z_l) + sigmoid(Gate_sem(Z_l,C_l,B,G))*CrossAttn(Z_l,S_t) + sigmoid(Gate_mem(Z_l,G,B))*CrossAttn(Z_l,M_t), with a bounded gate initialised slightly open (e.g. sigmoid(-2)). Delete MEMORY from fit_budget. Test: rel dZ with vs without M at least 5% after training on the delayed-cue task, and the gate value logs per layer

(2) Implement Retriever.memory_tokens(ids, now): recompute memory tokens with the ONLINE segment encoder from cached event features (see the Consolidator action) so model.memory_tokens (model.py:1044) has gradients in filter_sequence and policy_evaluate. Test: after one update, every segment_encoder parameter has a nonzero grad from the world and policy objectives and the backbone grad from memory is > 0

(3) Add objective_retrieval to agent.DEFAULT_OBJECTIVES. For each replayed decision t, take candidates = top-32 from the served index + 16 random + same-stream negatives. Compute utility u_c = L_t(M without c) - L_t(M with c) with Retriever.measure_usefulness, where L_t is the per-row world/outcome NLL plus value error from the CAM forward under no_grad, batched. Apply usefulness_loss(q=Q(Z_{t-1},G,B), keys, u, margin). Gradients go into query_net and key_head. Log pos_frac/acc. Test: grad on every query_net parameter > 0; capabilities/memory.py run_memory 'memory' condition reaches hit-rate >= 0.8 among >= 2,000 segments and accuracy >= chance + 0.3, run on the GPU stack

(4) Replace the default event encoder with an ActorView encoder over CAM's own tokenizer output (pooled frozen-semantic observation embeddings + action/result tokens), reading actor-visible fields only

(5) Detail recall: when a learned recall gate fires (or as an explicit CAM-internal memory action), fetch source records (archive.get) and artifacts and re-tokenize them as EVENT tokens for the next step. Test: an exact 7-digit amount seen 5,000 events earlier is reproduced in the action arguments
(6) Train long_encoder too (compression and usefulness over level-2 segments), or stop serving level-2 keys until it is trained

components.name: Consolidator + embedding versioning/migration (incl. CamUnifiedAgent._memory_sync)
components.evidence: p1: consolidated 200k events into 6,400 L1 + 800 L2 segments at 3,005 ev/s in 3 step() calls (max_events 100k each, so it lags but never drops). p4_migrate.py: initial consolidation 100 s. sync_target gave migration_pending=True. step() during the migration consumed 2,000 events into 64 L1 + 8 L2 segments, and retrieve() worked, but 0 of the 72 new segments were retrievable before promotion. A second sync was held back (reason 'migration-pending') and retrieve stayed OK. Wave-1's E02 failures are therefore fixed. The full re-encode (max_items=None, which is what agent.py:1074 calls) took 278.2 s for 202k events and 7,200 segments, about 1,377 s per 1M events and 13,773 s per 10M. p3: every sync re-encoded ALL segments (1, 3, 4, 6 at updates 1-4); stage1 default memory_sync_every=4 (stage1/system.py:79). p8_links.py: link_weights for 768 L1 + 256 L2 segments wrote 88,052 used-rows, 10.1 MB of archive budget, in 18.9 s per update.
defects: agent.py:1060-1079 _memory_sync: synchronous full re-encode inside update() every k updates. Cost is O(lifetime), so update latency grows without bound (an effective lifetime cutoff) - critical
consolidate.py:200-217 _encode1 / reencode re-reads raw Parquet records and re-featurizes them on every migration. No cached event features - major

actions: Cache per-event encoder input features once at ingest in a columnar store keyed by (gseq, feature_version) beside the index (fp16, e.g. 1536 x 2 B = 3 KB/event). Migrations then re-run only the segment and long encoders on cached features. Target: at least 50k segments/s re-encode

Budgeted incremental migration: _memory_sync calls con.reencode_step(max_items=c*new_segments + C0) every update and never max_items=None. Keep the previous target snapshot (prev_*) until promotion and dual-encode newly consolidated segments into both the served and pending versions so they are retrievable immediately. Optionally learn a key adapter old->new (spec 10.5 'compatible target encoders') to serve during migration
link_weights: segment-level weight_links rows only

Test 1: a 1M-event lifetime with sync every 4 updates keeps p95 update wall time within 2x of no-sync. Test 2: segments created during a migration appear in top-k for their own cue. Test 3: provenance at most 1 KB per update. Test 4: an index re-encoded from the cache equals one re-encoded from raw records (atol 1e-3)

components.name: Distributed-learning memory integration
components.evidence: dist/learner.py:706 defaults to sink_factory 'dist.sinks:make_jsonl_archive' (a separate JsonlArchive with its own StorageLimitExceeded). Grep finds no EventArchive, ReplaySampler, MemoryIndex or Consolidator anywhere in dist/. The distributed path therefore has no stratified persistent replay, no consolidation and no retrieval.
defects: Two archive implementations; the distributed learner bypasses all of E's lifetime memory - major
actions: Make the central learner the single EventArchive writer (the flock design fits) and have it run Consolidator and ReplaySampler. Actors open MemoryIndex(readonly=True) and retrieve against the index version broadcast with each weight version. Test: actor B's later retrieval returns a segment built from actor A's experience, and actor B's behaviour changes

requirements.justification: No ingestion cap anywhere in the real path (harness -> HarnessAgent -> CamUnifiedAgent._archive -> EventArchive). The archive streamed 200k events (5.8k ev/s, 392 B/event) and survived restart and SIGKILL with 0 acknowledged events lost; wave-1/2 measured 1M at component level. But the 1M stress was never run through the agent loop (the real runs have 6-12 decisions). O(lifetime) costs act as hidden cutoffs: full re-encode every 4 updates (278 s per 202k events), provenance linking at about 10 MB per update that exhausts the 200 GiB budget after about 20k updates, a full index copy per checkpoint, and an unbounded update_log.

Durability and restart are real (p1, p2). Retrieval is not learned in the runtime: query_net L2 change 0.0 and no gradient over 4 real updates, usefulness_loss never called outside tests, and memory values have no gradient (stored_memory_tokens is @no_grad). Wave-2 delayed-cue run through the complete architecture: hit-rate 0.0 after training (read, not reproduced).

Memory-side view only. In the real ow_tiny run the core's weights changed at every update (rel delta 0.0019 -> 0.0010; backbone grads from world/adapt/actor/value). The memory objective contributes 0.0 gradient to the backbone; memory tokens rebuilt in replay are gradient-free stored values. Core training is not yet at main scale.

Instruments are correct on toy networks. find_unit_layers finds 0 of the 8 fused SwiGLU layers of the UnifiedCore. Dormant units, rank, new-task speed and retention are not measured in the training runtime (only grad norms, cosines and param deltas via D's trainer and the harness). exp3 never ran beyond prepare.

On the real stack the weights-only file holds only parameters/buffers plus 4 metadata keys (1,069 tensors, 40 MB; no optimizer, RNG or replay). The fresh-process path is therefore clean. In-process load_weights_only on a used agent leaks the fresh buffer (source decisions get trained on), loss_mag, trainer n_updates/stage, trackers/option/last_actions/last_now and the RNG. Experience-derived state_norm running statistics are inside the file. All acceptance tests use the ToyAgent double. REPAIR required.

Archive, replay and consolidator recover correctly. Full-lifetime completeness depends on HarnessAgent._extra_state duplicating the CheckpointOps contract. Resume is evidenced only for a 6-decision run with no memory segments. Each checkpoint copies the whole memory index (O(index)).

The hierarchy (events -> L1 -> L2 -> artifact refs -> weight links) and its source links exist and run (7,200 segments from 200k events). The compression objective in runtime stayed at chance (2.21 vs 2.08). long_encoder is never trained (0.0 change) though its L2 keys are served. Compression is not trained for decision usefulness (spec 10.4). Originals are never re-injected into decisions.

Semantics are now correct (p4): step during migration, second sync held back, retrieve never raises, promotion drops the old version. Two defects remain: segments created during a migration cannot be retrieved until promotion (0/72), and migration is a synchronous full re-encode from raw records (about 23 min per 1M events) called every 4 updates. REDESIGN of the policy is required.

The stress parts pass (>256, >10k, 200k reproduced; 1M per wave-1). The 'arbitrary delayed cues using the complete CAM architecture' part failed in wave-2 Y's real-component run: accuracy 0.0 vs chance 0.25 in all conditions, and global retrieval hit-rate 0.047 -> 0.0 after 360 updates among 1,824 segments (result files read, not reproduced). The mechanism I measured explains it: the query is untrained and memory values carry no gradient.

The sampler infrastructure is correct and fast (sync 200k in 1.7 s, draw 64 x 16 in 0.25 s). In the real runtime innovations, rare and skills are always empty (no tag producers), domain equals env_id and failures equal ok=False. No outcome-anchored trajectory sampling.

Mechanisms exist behind switches and pass toy tests. None is wired into the CombinedTrainer or the runtime. CBP and ReDo cannot address the core's fused SwiGLU units. No controlled comparison in the integrated system. Context-dependent parameter use is absent.

archive.risks:
Measurement caveats:
- All real-stack measurements used tiny CAM widths (d_model 64, 2 layers) with Qwen3-0.6B. They cover 12 decisions per run and at most 6 memory segments. That shows wiring and gradient paths, not learning quality at scale.
- The context-budget pressure on MEMORY tokens (lowest priority) could not be exercised. It needs a large index plus entity-rich steps at the default 384 budget.
- Timings (re-encode 278 s, consolidation 2-3k ev/s, link_weights 18.9 s/update) were taken on a GPU and CPU shared with other auditors and are probably inflated. Their scaling with lifetime length (linear) is the finding, not the constants.
- The wave-2 Y delayed-cue failure was read from its result files, not reproduced.

Scale and design risks:
- At the DOM scale the retriever alone has 170.6M parameters, half of them frozen target copies stored in every weights file. Memory values cost 12 KB per segment, and re-encoding through a 768-wide encoder with semantic event features will be far slower than measured here. Without the feature cache and budgeted migration, the current _memory_sync design will stall training outright.
- In weights-only transfer conditions the retriever has no index, so the core is evaluated without the memory tokens it was trained with. This is a distribution shift that confounds B/C comparisons unless memory is a gated stream that tolerates absence.
- Parallel evaluation worlds can retrieve each other's segments (no default retrieval scoping).
- The state_norm running statistics in weights files are experience-derived. Decide whether they count as model parameters or as adaptive state before any transfer claim.
- Running the meta-learned-reward extension before the actor-view/label-ledger separation would leak evaluator-derived reward into actor inputs through memory, invalidating observation-only results.

h-core.subsystem: H-core: Core backbone F_theta, model assembly (CamUnifiedModel/build_model), latent reasoning, entities, invariance, config/scales, interfaces (TokenSet/TokenKind/FastState), DOM Mechanism C (core/semantic_xattn.py, added to the branch during this audit)
h-core.summary: The core is mechanically sound. F_theta (UnifiedCore) really is one shared backbone. The filter (encode_step, filter_sequence), world-model filter_step/transition/prior and the Reasoner all use the same core object, and the Reasoner reuses the last 4 blocks by identity (checked on the real build_model at every scale). Z_t is a persistent [B,S,D] state carried across decisions by the agent. build_model's DEFAULT_COMPONENT_PATHS build only real classes, with no doubles. Real gradients from the policy, the value head (after its zero-initialised output layer has taken one step) and the world-model loss reach the early, middle and late blocks. That also holds at the new 32x1536x24 scale with Qwen3-4B on GPU: block 0/16/31 gradient norms 0.38/0.38/2.22. The intelligence claims do not hold, though. (1) At initialisation Z_t is 99.5% a constant: cos(Z_t, state_pos+kind_emb) = 0.995. It depends on observation content by only about 2%, and information in Z decays by about 0.58x per decision. Under BPTT the ungated state cannot learn an 8-step delayed recall (7.8% vs 6.25% chance); a simple gated state update learns delays 8 and 16 at 100% within 100 iterations. (2) Reasoning does not change decisions in the real model. Forcing J=1..16 moves tool log-probs by at most 0.08 nats and the greedy actions are identical. In the wave-2 integrated capability runs (on the tiny 2x64 capability config), forced J changed 0% of decisions, KL under permuting R across rows was 4e-9, and the core's actor gradient was about 1000x smaller than the tokenizer's (3.8e-6 vs 3.0e-3). A03 has failed empirically. The root cause is architectural: the action generator's decision query reads raw tokenizer goal tokens, the tool logits include an R-independent tool_prior over raw tool tokens, and the pointers attend over raw observation and tool tokens, so the policy can bypass CAM's latent state. Mechanism B (an intent bottleneck) does not exist and this pathway must be redesigned. (3) The world-model loss gives zero gradient to the reasoning state (reasoner tensors 0/4), contrary to spec 4.3. (4) Replay filtering always starts slices from z0 even mid-episode, so training and acting state distributions differ. (5) Mechanism C (GatedUnifiedCore) is correct in isolation (4/4 unit tests pass) but is not wired into build_model, the tokenizer or encode_step. Its module-state design (set_semantic) crashes on imagination batches and silently corrupts gradients under the Reasoner's iteration checkpointing (141% gradient error). The manifest's DOM-01 figure of 1.081B therefore counts 170M parameters that no objective trains. The runtime core at the superlearner scale is 911M and is genuinely trained. The full runtime CAM is 1.47B trainable without the retriever, 1.56B with it, and about 1.73B with cross-attention, because the satellites scale with d_model. Fitting an AdamW step next to Qwen3-4B and the fp32 EMA target needs roughly 38-42 GB before activations. Entities and invariance work as libraries. Entity type tokens and invariance training are never used in the runtime, and spec 3.3 event tokens do not exist.

components.name: CamUnifiedModel decision pathway (step assembly encode_step/decide/policy_evaluate + action-generator conditioning; Mechanism B bottleneck)
components.evidence: The decision is computed by ActionGenerator._forward from decision_context(R, goal, belief) (actions.py:300). goal = [raw tokenizer GOAL tokens; OPTION; BUDGET] (model.py:1158-1169). The tool logits add tool_prior(tools2.x), an R-independent function of the raw tool tokens (actions.py:326). The tool and evidence pointers attend over raw tokenizer TOOL tokens and raw O_t (model.py:1365 passes enc.obs, not the core's ctx_out). The policy can therefore solve tasks without CAM's latent: KL under R permutation 4.2e-9 in the trained integrated agent; the core gets an actor gradient of 3.8e-6 vs 3.0e-3 for the tokenizer; in my dev run R noise of 1x std moved logp by <=0.05 nats. There is no intent representation I_t anywhere (grep 'intent' finds only config/bridge/heads docstrings and the unwired semantic/decoder_xattn.py). The decoder is conditioned only by a 16-vector soft prefix (bridge.py). Value: the ValueHead output layer is zero-initialised (learn/heads.py:91-93,165), so at step 0 the value gradient into the core is exactly 0 (only 2/13 value-head tensors); after one SGD step it reaches core blocks (382/1217/1219), the reasoner (339) and the tokenizer (1935). Superlearner scale on GPU (Qwen3-4B, use_memory False): 16.46 GB after build; decide B=4 0.49 s warm (2.69 s cold), peak 18.8 GB; policy_evaluate fwd+bwd 1.49 s, peak 25.8 GB (no optimizer); imagination decide with 4 candidates x 2 samples x horizon 2 takes 3.2 s (peak 19.7 GB). The default 8x4x4 extrapolates to about 25 s per decision.

semantic/actions.py:326 - tool_prior(tools2.x) adds R-independent tool logits - major

model.py:1365 and planner model.py:1782 - pointers/evidence over raw tokenizer obs/tool tokens instead of CAM-processed tokens; no CAM intent I_t; CAM never evaluates the concrete action as an authorization gate (only scores it inside the optional planner) - critical (Mechanism B)
model.py:1383 - Z_hat from enc.Z (not R); value V(R, raw G) - minor
learn/heads.py:91-93 - zero-init value output blocks all value gradient into CAM at step 0 (benign after one step, but DOM-08 checks must account for it) - minor
actions: Add Intent_theta in model.py: I_t = n_intent (e.g. 16-32) learned queries cross-attending to [R_t; ctx_out(O,M,B,G processed by the core)] via CrossBlock (core/blocks.py:142); new TokenKind.INTENT. ActionGenerator.sample/log_prob take I_t instead of (R, goal, belief): the tool reader, typed heads, LatentBridge and (later) decoder cross-attention all read only I_t. Goal and belief reach the decision only through Z/R/I.

Remove tool_prior or make it a bilinear function of I_t; feed TOOL tokens into the core context (so ctx_out at tool positions is state-conditioned) and use those as pointer keys; run the evidence pointer over ctx_out at observation positions (refs are preserved by fit_budget).

Concrete-action evaluation before execution: after decoding, compute A_tok -> world_model.prior(Z_t, A_tok, B_t, dt) -> Q(Z_hat, G) with CAM's own value; record it in Decision and reject/resample below a learned threshold (authorization flag checked by the env adapter).

Tests: (1) zeroing I_t yields a tool distribution independent of the goal text (bypass closed by construction); (2) DOM Condition G: swap R/I between rows whose goals require different tools; after imitation training the executed actions follow the donor in >= 90% of rows; (3) KL(pi | I permuted) > 0.1 nats after training; (4) DOM-08 gradient test after one optimizer step: nonzero gradients on core blocks 0/L/2/L-1, intent module, bridge/decoder xattn, LoRA B matrices, reasoner, beliefs, exploration head and value head from the combined loss.

components.name: Replay filter (filter_sequence) vs acting state
components.evidence: filter_sequence always starts from Z0 = core.init_state (model.py:1629). ReplaySampler slices start uniformly anywhere inside an episode (memory/replay.py:379-383); the agent's default seq_len is 8 (agent.py:386). So world/adapt/memory objectives train F on state trajectories that begin at z0 mid-episode, while acting uses the Z accumulated since the episode start. policy_evaluate uses the stored detached Z_{t-1} (one-step truncated BPTT), consistent with acting. Real 3-step SequenceBatch built from real decisions and observe_outcomes: world_loss 39.29 total; gradients reach every block (15.1/14.6/16.1), tokenizer 26/26 tensors, entity encoder 40/42, beliefs 20/40, outcome head 29/33, world model 207/223.
defects: model.py:1629 - replay filter starts mid-episode slices from z0: train/act state-distribution mismatch, and Z can never learn dependencies longer than seq_len=8 - major
actions: Burn-in (R2D2-style): sample burn_in + seq_len records (burn_in 16-32) and run the first burn_in filter steps under torch.no_grad before the graded steps; alternatively store bf16 Z snapshots every k decisions in EventRecord.extra and restart from the nearest one (393 KB per snapshot at superlearner scale).

Test: for an archived episode, filter_sequence on a slice starting at step 20 with burn-in 16 reproduces the acting Decision.Z at the slice's first graded step within 5% relative error (currently it starts from z0).

world.subsystem: World model, outcomes, imagination, planner, causal (world/*.py, capabilities/imagination.py, capabilities/causal.py; spec Parts 6, 7, 13.4; manifest A07 A08 C01 C02 C03 C04 C05 W03)
world.summary:
The mechanics are real, but the claimed capabilities rest on the DoubleCore test double and the HypothesisBelief/threshold-policy doubles. In the assembled real stack the world model has learned nothing that depends on the action or on observations.

**What holds up:**
- The transition is stochastic (categorical latent fed in as NOISE tokens) and conditioned on the action, and it runs on the same backbone as the filter.
- The multistep loss is genuinely open-loop. Prior samples and recorded actions are used and no future observations are read. Two small leaks exist: recorded future durations, and the future y_mask in imagined belief updates.
- Imagination clones the FastState per branch, updates it with imagined outcomes, re-runs the reasoner and samples the next action from the revised belief. This happens both in C's Imagination and in the runtime LatentImaginationPlanner.
- The runtime planner does pick the real action: all Stage-1 smoke decisions are source=cam_planner.

**What fails, measured:**
- **Y's integrated causal run (real Qwen tokenizer + UnifiedCore):**
  - Tests 1 to 5 of 6.6 fail. Action contrast is 0.0086. Delay-world predictions are flat at about 0.22 (max error 0.78). Interaction contrast is -3.8e-5 against a truth of 2.0. The switch gap is 4.8e-5.
  - On held-out data the world model scores about the same as key-mean. It loses to linear regression at every horizon (delay h2-4: 0.10 vs 0.0013).
- **The integrated 7.4 diagnostic fails:**
  - After training, the planner makes the same choice as the policy (changed_vs_policy 0.0) and both always play safe, for a return of 3.0 against 10 achievable.
  - The candidates never include run_test.
  - The predicted launch reward is the same whether the test came back positive or negative (-0.86 vs -0.88).
- **The EMA latent target is never updated in the real runtime.** Only the capabilities adapter calls update_target.

**Root causes I measured:**
1. The real tokenizer is nearly blind to numeric values. Token cosine for a signal of +1 vs -1 is 0.984; for points 0 vs 10 it is 0.995. In a synthetic replica with the same geometry (E7), the world model learns nothing from observed values (gap 0.0 against truth 2.0). With normal geometry the gap is 1.19. Action-token similarity (cosine 0.93) is not the problem (E6 passes).
2. The KL term gives no gradient. At convergence the KL is 0.31-0.36 nats, below kl_free_nats=1.0, so the clamp zeroes the gradient and the prior is trained only by the open-loop terms.
3. Deterministic delayed effects get explained as latent noise. In the failing run (seed 5) the sampled forecast is 0.59, the mode-latent forecast is 0.00, and prior entropy is about 9 nats per step in a world with 0.05 noise. The delayed-effect test is therefore flaky. The current fix is more steps plus LR decay, which treats the symptom. The switch test also failed in my run.
4. Imagined states are off the posterior manifold. MSE(Z^, Z_post) divided by Var(Z_post) is 0.17-0.49 when trained, and 0.74-1.35 at 450 steps. Value, reasoner and policy heads are therefore evaluated out of distribution during imagination.

**What is not wired in:** C's planners (beam / CEM / policy-rollout), imagine_train, CausalLedger/CausalProvenance and InterventionContrastive are not used by the runtime.

**Scale:** at the 1B scale a full-core transition costs 277 GFLOP per row, about 1.5 PFLOP per world-model update at T=32, and 71-142 TFLOP per planned decision. It also needs a second 911M EMA copy. With DOM-C the transition runs without semantic states while the filter runs with them.

**Bottom line:** keep the outcome head, the open-loop machinery and the baselines. Redesign the dynamics/filter coupling and the planner. Implement observation-only utility, VOI and the RUDDER/COCOA services.

components.name: WorldModel dynamics: filter, prior/posterior transition, open-loop loss (world/dynamics.py)
components.evidence:
Read dynamics.py in full and traced model.decide (model.py:1356-1388), world_loss (model.py:1667-1675) and stage1/system.py.

Structure:
- prior/transition (dynamics.py:313-343) calls the shared core with [A; B; TIME; NOISE(z)].
- The open loop (dynamics.py:743-837) uses prior samples and recorded actions only.

Y's integrated run on the real stack (evidence Y/exp/causal_s0.json, 300 world-only steps):
- t1 mean_abs_pairwise_diff = 0.0086.
- t2 predictions are 0.221-0.234 for every plan (truth 1/0/1); max_abs_err 0.776.
- t3 predicts 0.0813 for all 4 lever settings; contrast -3.8e-5 against truth 2.0 (linear regression: 0.197).
- t4 switch vs no-switch gap 4.8e-5.
- t5 delay MSE: world model 0.096/0.103/0.111/0.105, linear regression 0.038/0.0013/0.0013/0.0012. The world model is about equal to key-mean (0.090-0.099).

My experiments:
- E1, synthetic DelayWorld on the real UnifiedCore (700 steps, LR decay): passes, max error 0.022. The core is not the problem.
- E4, real tokenizer at initialisation: changing the action moves Z_hat by MSD 1.05e-7, against an across-row variance of 1.85e-5.
- E3/E3b, prior-vs-posterior gap MSE(Z^_{t+1}, Z_post_{t+1}) / Var(Z_post): 0.17 (DoubleCore, 700 steps), 0.49 (UnifiedCore, 700 steps), 0.74-1.35 at 450 steps.
- E5, cost at the superlearner scale (meta-device count): core 911.3M, EMA target 911.3M, world-model heads 150.5M; 277 GFLOP forward per transition row; T=32, B=2 open loop = 1824 rows, about 1.5 PFLOP per update; planning n8/s4/h8 = 71 TFLOP, h16 = 142 TFLOP per decision.
defects: world/dynamics.py:313-319 - the transition is a full pass of the shared core per imagined row. At 1B scale that is 277 GFLOP per row and about 1.5 PFLOP per update at T=32 (needs about 42 GB+ of activations without checkpointing); planning h8-h16 costs 71-142 TFLOP per decision - critical

world/dynamics.py:244-249 / 252-272 - the world model's own filter calls core(Z, ctx) without semantic states. With DOM-C GatedUnifiedCore (core/semantic_xattn.py) acting runs with S_t but the world-model filter and the prior do not: train/act mismatch - critical

world/dynamics.py:540-542 + model.py:1667-1675 - world_loss ignores filt.Zs and re-runs its own filter (online + EMA). Together with model.filter_sequence that is 3 core passes per update over a context assembled differently from encode_step (fit_budget vs the core's select_budget) - major

world/dynamics.py:391 - the latent target is matched through a residual MLP (p = Zh + latent_pred(Zh)), so nothing ties Z^ to Z_post. Measured gap 0.17-1.35 x Var(Z_post); every head applied to imagined states is out of distribution - critical

world/dynamics.py:765-766 + model.py:1667-1675 - the agent's world loss never passes fast_states / belief_update_fn, so open-loop belief tokens stay frozen at B_t while the runtime planner updates beliefs every imagined step: train/imagine mismatch - major
world/dynamics.py:501-507 - horizons > T are skipped. Stage-1 seq_len=8 and the capability runs use T=3-8, so horizons 16 and 32 are never trained - major
world/dynamics.py:788 - recorded future durations dt_{t+k} are fed into the open-loop rollout (duration can depend on the outcome); imagination uses predicted durations instead - minor
world/dynamics.py:796-803 - the imagined belief update uses the real future y_mask (which outcomes were observed) - minor
integrated: no action- or observation-conditioned prediction is learned in the real stack (Y causal_s0: t1 0.0086, t3 contrast -3.8e-5, t4 gap 4.8e-5) - critical
actions:
Split the transition from the filter:
- Keep the full GatedUnifiedCore with S_t cross-attention as the filter/posterior encoder Z_post_t.
- Add a dedicated latent dynamics transformer T_phi: 6-8 blocks at width d_model, over the 128 state tokens plus [A; B; TIME; NOISE; G] context, without semantic cross-attention, about 150-250M params. It shares kind/time embeddings with the core and may reuse the last k core blocks the way the Reasoner does.
- Test: superlearner scale, B=1, n=8, s=4, h=8 planning in under 1.5 s on the A6000 (time it with torch.cuda.Event).

Add a state-consistency loss L_cons = mean(((Z^_{t+1} - sg(Z_post_{t+1})) / sd(Z_post))^2) on the teacher-forced posterior-latent transition and on open-loop h=1. Optionally go RSSM-style (Z_post_{t+1} = Core(Z^_{t+1}, [O_{t+1}; S_{t+1}])), so posterior states are corrections of prior states.
- Test: the E3 metric prior_vs_post_state_mse / Var(Z_post) is under 0.1 on DelayWorld and on integrated DelayEffectEnv; |V(Z^) - V(Z_post)| is under 10% of std(V).

Single filter: change WorldModel.loss to accept Z_post (with gradients) and the matching ctx builder from model.filter_sequence (which already includes S_t, entity, option and memory tokens); compute the EMA target with the same context builder and the target core. Remove WorldModel.filter from the agent path.
- Test: an assertion that world_loss's Z_post equals encode_step's Z_t on replayed records to within 1e-5.

Pass fast_states plus beliefs.update/tokens into the agent's world loss (bel_dyn path), so open-loop belief tokens evolve as in imagination.
- Test: test_imagination_consistent_open_loop_uses_only_sampled_outcomes, extended to the real BeliefModule.

Replay sequence length must be at least max(train_horizons)+1 (33). Use truncated starts: detach the start state for h >= 8 to bound memory.
- Test: horizons_trained == (1,2,4,8,16,32) in Stage-1 logs.

components.name: KL free nats and stochastic-latent credit (delayed-effect learning reliability; test_learns_delayed_versus_immediate_effects)
components.evidence:
Y's sweeps (evidence Y/delay):
- 450 steps, constant LR: 1 of 6 fail.
- 450 steps with LR decay: 4 of 6 fail (delayed 0.518-0.648).
- 600-700 steps with LR decay: 18 of 18 pass.
- Learning curves keep dropping back (curve_m0 step 800: delayed 0.19).

Y's fix (more steps plus LR decay) treats the symptom. My measurements:
- E1: at convergence kl_value is 0.363 (DoubleCore) and 0.313 (UnifiedCore), below kl_free_nats=1.0; reported kl is 1.002 (clamped), so the KL gradient is zero.
- E2, kl_free_nats=0, 450 steps with decay, seeds 0/1/2: max error 0.425/0.016/0.007. Y's runs of the same recipe and seeds failed at 0.352/0.352/0.482, so 2 of 3 are rescued.
- E3, failing seed 5: forecast mean 0.667 (64-sample 0.587), mode-latent forecast 0.000, 78% of samples in [0.2, 0.8], prior entropy 9.1-9.4 nats per step (world noise 0.05). The delayed effect is carried by latent noise, not by the deterministic path.
- E3b, passing models: prior entropy still 2.8-13.6 nats per step.
- My run of test_world_learning.py: delay test passed (700 steps). test_predictions_follow_a_mechanism_change... FAILED (450 steps, constant LR): mirrored episode -0.14..-0.31 against the >0.7 threshold.
defects: world/dynamics.py:573-575 - the free-nats clamp is applied to the KL total summed over groups (1.0 nat). Below it the gradient is exactly zero, so the prior is never trained by KL in near-deterministic worlds (measured KL 0.31-0.36) - major

world/dynamics.py:673-709 - the trajectory mixture credit with open_loop_samples=2 forgives up to ln 2 per trajectory, so a deterministic delayed effect can be represented as a 50/50 latent coin - major
world/dynamics.py:755-758 - open_loop_starts=4 in the tests (8 by default) gives few h>=2 training rows - minor
tests/cam_unified/world/test_world_learning.py:188-198 - the switch test runs on a single seed at 450 steps with constant LR; it failed in my run - major
actions:
Replace the total free-nats clamp with per-group free bits of about 0.02-0.05 nats/group (sum <= 0.2 for 32x32) or kl_free_nats <= 0.1.
- Test: DelayWorld at 450 steps with decay passes on 6 of 6 seeds.

Add a mode-latent open-loop term: one of the S samples uses the prior mode (straight-through) and is scored with weight 1/S outside the mixture, so deterministic effects must sit on the deterministic path. Add a small prior-entropy penalty when the posterior KL is under 0.05.
- Test: the E3 metric 'pred_mode_latent' row-2 h3 > 0.7 on every seed; prior entropy < 2 nats/step on DelayWorld.
Use every start (open_loop_starts=None) for T <= 32 and open_loop_samples >= 4.

Make every 6.6 learning test multi-seed (6 seeds; all pass, or >= 5/6 with a fixed lower bound), add LR decay to the switch/interaction recipes, and assert both the sampled and the mode-latent forecasts.

requirements.justification: The structure is real: stochastic categorical-latent transition on the shared core, action/belief/dt conditioning, and typed likelihoods verified against torch.distributions. Learning succeeds only with the DoubleCore double; E1 also shows it with synthetic tokens on UnifiedCore. In the real integrated stack the predictions do not depend on the action or on observations: Y causal_s0 t1 mean pairwise action difference 0.0086, t2 flat 0.22-0.23 (max error 0.78), t3 contrast -3.8e-5 vs 2.0, t4 gap 4.8e-5. The delayed-effect test is seed-flaky: KL below free nats gives a zero KL gradient, and the effect gets carried by latent noise (mode-latent forecast 0.00 in a failing seed). My run of the switch test failed.

Mechanics are implemented and in the runtime: FastState clones, imagined belief/Kalman updates, the reasoner re-run, the next action from the revised belief, and argmax selection of the real action (Stage-1 smoke runs are all source=cam_planner). Only h=2 was ever run end to end. In Y's integrated ProbeEnv runs the trained planner never changes the action relative to the policy (changed_vs_policy 0.0; play_safe 100%, return 3.0 vs 10). Its candidates never contain the experiment, the world model ignores the observed signal, and imagined states are off the posterior manifold.

The open loop is genuine, with minor leaks: recorded future dt and future y_mask. It beats the baselines only on synthetic StockWorld with DoubleCore (h <= 8). On real recorded integrated sequences (Y causal_s0 t5) the world model is about equal to key-mean and loses to linear regression at all h on delay (0.096/0.103/0.111/0.105 vs 0.038/0.0013/0.0013/0.0012). On switch it loses to no-change at h1-2 (0.27 vs 0.10). Horizons 16/32 are never trained (seq_len 8).

CausalLedger and CausalProvenance are implemented and unit-tested, but they are not wired: no runtime EventRecord gets randomization_p/simultaneous/attributed_to, and EVENT tokens never receive the features.

Y implemented all seven 6.6 tests on the real stack (capabilities/causal.py) and ran them (causal_s0.json). Tests 1-5 fail; 6 passes partly via the belief/Kalman path (0.52 difference); 7 passes (isolation, bit-identical FastState). They are not in pytest.

Beam/CEM/policy-rollout with correct matched-budget accounting and imagine_train exist and pass unit/slow tests on doubles. None of them is reachable from the runtime (no PlannerP adapter; imagine_train is not used by the trainer).

The costly-experiment diagnostic exists in both a synthetic version (ProbeWorld with doubles: passes at h=2) and an integrated version (ProbeEnv via capabilities/imagination.py). The integrated runs (imagination_s0/_es/_film02/_std/_ent/_ingest) fail: after training, policy and planner always play safe, the enumerated test-minus-safe margin is -0.25..+0.05, and the post-test launch prediction is identical for +/- signals.
InterventionContrastive is implemented with passing isolated synthetic tests, but it is not part of any optimised objective.

world.risks:
1. **Dynamics cost at the 1B scale.** The full-core transition at 277 GFLOP/row makes open-loop training to h=32 and planning at h=8-16 unaffordable on one A6000: about 1.5 PFLOP per update and 71-142 TFLOP per decision. The 911M EMA copy doubles core memory. A dedicated dynamics module changes the 'shared transition' reading of spec 6.1, so declare the deviation: transition parameters shared with or initialised from the core's top blocks.
2. **DOM-C mismatch.** With GatedUnifiedCore the filter runs with semantic cross-attention but the world-model filter and transition run without it. Until there is one shared filter, world-model heads are trained on different states than the ones used for acting.
3. **Imagination states are out of distribution** for the value, policy, R_psi and ProspectEvaluator heads (measured gap 0.17-1.35 x Var). Training the policy from imagination before the consistency fix invites exploitation of model errors.
4. **Tokenizer dependency.** Workstream A's numeric value-blindness alone blocks observation-conditioned world-model learning (E7). World-model fixes will not show integrated gains until the tokenizer value channel is fixed.
5. **Unexplained remainder.** The integrated delay-world failure is not fully explained: the core, action-token geometry and, for the immediate effect, training budget are ruled out. The remaining suspects are real obs-token swamping, the many-query outcome spec, BeliefModule tokens and CombinedTrainer settings. Run the ablation ladder first; this may surface more defects.
6. **Flaky learning tests.** Non-deterministic CUDA kernels make single-seed learning tests flaky (the delay test historically, the switch test failed in my run). Acceptance needs multi-seed criteria.
7. **Observation-only mode.** The current planner objective collapses to argmax V, so any OpenWorld result under use_imagination=True without the R_psi/success hooks is uninformative.
8. **Calendar.** The rental ends 2026-11-30 03:00 UTC. Integrated runs with Qwen contend for the shared GPU lock: my E4 waited more than 10 minutes for it.

distributed.subsystem: Distributed actor-learner (superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/dist/*; spec Part 14, A16, F01-F04, X06; meta-reward Part 13 / CD-01)
distributed.summary:
The real CAM actor-learner path exists and works at TINY scale. Each actor runs a full CamUnifiedModel (Qwen3-0.6B, 1.9M-param core) on a real process-isolated ow_tiny world and writes to the durable spool. The central CamLearnerModel recomputes the behaviour log-probability (lag-0 deviation 0.0 nats in-process) and takes an optimiser step. Atomic weights-only publication follows, and the other actors refresh at decision boundaries.

I ran two checks myself.
- In-process counterfactual: one update trained only on actor0's 6 decisions. Under it actor1 (different seed and world) took 6 of 6 different actions (5 of 6 different tools) compared with the same actor1 under v0. A v0 repeat was identical (0 of 6), so the sampling is deterministic.
- Real 4-process run (learner trained on actor0 only, 240 s): actors 1-3 adopted v1..v15, which were trained only on actor0's data. Totals: 408 decisions, 1.60 decisions/s, learner 0.45 trained decisions/s, trained lags {0:7, 1:60, 2:28, 3:1}, 90 of 96 trained decisions went through V-trace.

So the A16 mechanism is integration-tested with real CAM. The change in behaviour is not learning, though:
- mean training reward is 0.0 (about 1e-6 of stale learning-progress bonus);
- the policy's share of the backbone gradient is 1.7e-5 to 8e-5 against 0.90-0.92 for the world loss;
- the actions are degenerate (behaviour logp -5 to -89 nats, e.g. jobs.close / id.remove with made-up arguments).

The distribution infrastructure is sound and should be kept: queue/WAL/dedup/backpressure, the atomic LATEST protocol, per-decision lag routing, assembler segments and launcher supervision. 65 non-GPU tests pass.

Four architectural assumptions break under the new requirements:
1. Every actor holds its own full model copy on the GPU and refreshes from files. At 1B core plus Qwen3-4B that is about 14 GB per actor. Measured publication at 1.2B fp32: 30-55 s per version, 15 s per actor fetch, 35 GB publisher RSS. With publish_every=1 this cannot work. A central batched inference server sharing the learner's single frozen Qwen copy is required.
2. The training reward is the evaluator's take_rewards increment, and it is also fed into the actor's beliefs. This is incompatible with observation_only and violates the channel separation.
3. Every decision is trained exactly once from the stream: no replay, late outcomes and labels dropped. This cannot support RUDDER, COCOA, hindsight relabelling or meta-gradients.
4. Intrinsic learning-progress reward, FastState and z0 are reused stale. No reward-model, evaluator or environment versions exist (CD-01 not started).

The CAM learner also uses the toy's validated max lag (32) by default because lag_validation_cam.json does not exist.

Add a LabelJoiner: the labels/ spool feeds a per-(env_id, episode, goal) label table with status PENDING/SUCCESS/FAILURE/UNCERTAIN; when a label resolves, the episode becomes eligible for retrospective batches.

Add a ReplaySampler producing typed batches: fresh (lag <= validated L, for policy), replay (any lag, for world/self-eval/predictors, from E's archive replay, memory/), retrospective (newly labelled episodes, for RUDDER F_xi / COCOA hindsight / success predictors), and meta pairs (inner and query batches disjoint by episode, for psi).

Add a TrainingCheckpoint every K updates: weights + CombinedTrainer.state_dict() (learn/trainer.py:328) + psi and its optimiser + RNG + sampler cursors + the pending-label table; resume from it, not from LATEST weights.

Tests: (1) kill the learner and resume: the next update's loss and parameters match an uninterrupted run within 1e-6; (2) a label released after its decisions were trained produces a retrospective update touching those event_ids; (3) the replay sampler's domain balance matches its configured weights.

components.name: CAM learner model (CamLearnerModel)
components.evidence: Real integration: the exact StepInputs are read from the content-addressed InputsStore, the latent state is re-filtered under the current weights, and policy_evaluate recomputes the joint logp. x1: lag-0 deviation 0.0, 6 decisions trained in 26.2 s (state 6.1 s, policy_eval 11.5 s, world 4.5 s, step 4.1 s). mp4b: 9.9 s per 6-decision update, 1.65 s per trained decision, about 0.45 trained decisions/s. Gradient budget: x1 backbone share actor 1.7e-5 / world 0.92 / adapt 0.077; mp4b update 1: actor 8.3e-5 / world 0.896; smoke: world loss 3471 vs actor -0.157, share 0.99985, grad norm 23512 clipped. mean_reward 0.0 in x1 and about 1e-6 in mp4b. World loss fell 30.1 to 20.5 over 16 updates, so world-model learning, not policy learning, drives the cross-actor behaviour change.
defects: cam_learner.py:318: the reward is e.reward, i.e. the evaluator's take_rewards increments (actor.py:344-352). In observation_only this is 0 and there is no R_psi, so IR-02 is unmet
cam_learner.py:317: stale actor-side intrinsic learning progress (lp_prev)
cam_learner.py:231: a from-start piece is re-filtered from the stored Z_prev (z0 under the behaviour version), not m.core.init_state(1), even though z0 is learned (core/backbone.py:96-99)
FastState (beliefs, Kalman) used in recomputation is the actor's stored snapshot (cam_policy.py:216-218), built under old weights and never recomputed
cam_learner.py:258: Z inputs are detached, so there is no gradient through time into the recurrent state (one-step credit only) - relevant to DOM (E)

cam_learner.py:257-284, 420: policy_rows=1 forwards (B=1) and all graphs kept until one backward; memory grows as O(batch x activations), which will OOM at 1B core + Qwen3-4B decoder with cross-attention gradients
The batch's trajectory outcomes (tr.outcomes) and late outcomes (batch.late_outcomes) are ignored
The world loss scale swamps the policy gradient in the shared backbone (D/C issue, but it decides whether the distributed learning is reward learning)
actions: Reward: compute r_t = R_psi(b_t, e_a, b_next, e_g, signals; psi_current) with selfeval/intrinsic.py IntrinsicReward inside update(), with b_t, b_next and e_a recomputed under the current theta. Use e.reward only when run.reward_mode is a declared legacy baseline; assert reward_mode=='observation_only' otherwise. Log psi_version per update.

Recompute FastState along each piece by replaying observe_outcomes (beliefs.update + kalman_update) from the stored realised outcome specs, or tag fast_version and treat a mismatch as off-policy (never 'exact').
For pieces with from_start=True, start from m.core.init_state(1).
Add optional truncated BPTT over burn-in plus segment (k steps, not detached) for core and state gradients, gated by config.

Micro-batch backward: evaluate policy_rows=8-16 rows per chunk and call backward per chunk with loss/n scaling (CombinedTrainer needs an accumulate API). Drop the B=1 exactness requirement: importance ratios absorb numerical noise, and |log pi - log mu| at lag 0 stays a diagnostic with a threshold of 0.05 nats.
Feed tr.outcomes, late outcomes and LabelJoiner labels into the self-evaluation and credit heads (selfeval/evaluator.py, credit/heads.py) through the replay and retrospective batches.
Rebalance the losses (per-token world loss normalisation or per-objective gradient-norm targets) so the policy share of the backbone gradient is at least 1%.

Tests: (a) observation_only run: a reward tensor equal to R_psi_new after a psi bump; (b) gradient presence in early/middle/late core layers from L_policy alone (DOM E); (c) 1B core + Qwen3-4B update with 32 decisions fits within 30 GB.

components.name: CAM actor policy (one full model copy per actor process)
components.evidence: Each actor process builds the full CamUnifiedModel including its own Qwen (cam_policy.py:336). mp4b: peak GPU 3.1 GB per process, 12.45 GB summed over 5 processes at TINY + Qwen3-0.6B. Acting cost: act 2.25 s/decision/actor (mp4b), 3.38 s in-process (x1). Smoke: 828 Qwen decoder steps for 24 decisions, about 97 ms per step at B=1; observe 0.23-0.59 s/decision. batch_invariant forces max_batch_tokens=1 and math-only SDPA (cam_policy.py:96-97, 67-76), so there is no batching. DIST_DEFAULTS (cam_policy.py:52) turn off imagination and memory and cap arguments at 32 tokens, so the distributed CAM has no planner and no CAM evaluation of the concrete action before execution (DOM B). rebuild_state replaces only Z (cam_policy.py:473-474), not FastState. Probe: make_cam_policy(semantic=...) raises TypeError, so CAM cannot use semserve. Projection at superlearner scale: Qwen3-4B bf16 about 8 GB + 1.0-1.2B core fp32 about 4.5 GB + KV and activations, about 13-14 GB per actor. At most 3 actors fit on 48 GB, with no room for the learner (about 30+ GB).
defects: cam_policy.py:336: a per-process full model copy does not scale to 1B + 4B on one GPU
cam_policy.py:52: imagination and memory disabled, max_arg_tokens=32 (code.commit about 1068 tokens is impossible)
cam_policy.py:96-97: B=1 encoder chunks; decoding at B=1 in every actor
cam_policy.py:449-477: the latent rebuild ignores the beliefs (FastState), so the spec 14.3 'no stale latent state' is only half met
Per-decision artifact (Z_prev fp32 etc.): about 14 KB at TINY. At superlearner scale Z_prev alone is 128x1536x4 B = 786 KB per decision, about 0.8 TB per 1M decisions (221 GB of disk free)
actions: Move acting into the central inference server (next component). Keep pack_step_inputs/unpack_step_inputs, InputsStore, alias_map/unique_state_dict/load_unique_state_dict (they become server-side).

Store Z_prev only at segment anchors (every segment_len decisions) in bf16; the learner already re-filters from the first event of a piece. Test: recompute deviation at lag 0 under 0.05 nats with anchors only.
Rebuild FastState together with Z in rebuild_state (replay observe_outcomes over the window).
Re-enable use_imagination/use_memory in the distributed config once behaviour provenance records the candidate distribution (see CD-01).

components.name: Central batched CAM inference server (required for the 1B core + Qwen3-4B)
components.evidence: Nothing exists for CAM. semserve.py (Qwen-only hidden/embed/generate with a soft prefix, request queue + per-client reply queues, batching window, versions swapped only between batches) is a usable transport and batching skeleton, but it holds no CAM core, no per-session state, and no Z-conditioned multi-layer decoder cross-attention (DOM A). Memory budget on one A6000 if learner and inference share one process and one frozen Qwen3-4B: Qwen 8 GB + core master fp32 4.5 GB + AdamW 9 GB + grads 4.5 GB + bf16 inference copy 2.3 GB + activations with checkpointing about 8 GB, about 36 GB. Separate processes would duplicate Qwen and exceed the budget.
defects: Not implemented; DOM-13 (full OpenWorld learning with 1B + Qwen3-4B) is blocked on it
actions: Add dist/infer.py with CamInferenceServer(model, max_batch=32, max_wait_ms=5). Sessions are keyed by (actor_id, env_id, episode_id), and their CamState rows (Z, FastState, registries, option, trackers, budget, rebuild window) stay on the GPU; use CamState.select/scatter (model.py:586).

Ops: open(actor_id, env_ids, goals, tools) returns sids; decide(sid, obs, tools, now, budget) returns Action + behaviour provenance; observe(sid, results, next_obs) returns [(EventRecord, DecisionTrace)]; close(sid, reason). Requests from many actors are batched into one model.decide, with batched Qwen decoding and per-row KV cache (semantic/encoder.py:419).

Add InferenceClient implementing actor.RecordPolicyP (reset/act_batch/observe_batch/end_episode; load_weights and rebuild_state are no-ops because the server manages them). ActorProcess becomes a CPU-only env shell (cuda=False).

Run the learner thread and the inference loop in one process (two CUDA streams), sharing the frozen Qwen3-4B. Version swap between batches by copying master to bf16; per-session drift is tracked server-side, with batched Z+FastState rebuild above the threshold.
The server stamps every record with policy, state and fast versions and inference_server_id. Records go back to the actor, which writes them to its WAL/queue (durability stays at the actor).

Tests: (1) a batched decide over 8 sessions from 4 clients gives logp within 0.05 nats of per-row decide; (2) a swap never occurs inside a batch (all records of a batch share model_version); (3) a client SIGKILL closes its sessions and the actor's next incarnation opens new ones; (4) at superlearner scale + Qwen3-4B with 16 sessions, learner + server peak under 40 GB; (5) throughput at dev scale with 16 sessions at least 10x the current 0.4 decisions/s/actor.

components.name: Actor process / SMDP harness (ActorProcess)
components.evidence: The harness works with the CAM records policy: event-seq deduplication across execute/advance/collect, incarnations, WAL, closing of the previous incarnation's open episodes, and decision-boundary refresh. mp4b: 4 actors, 0 env failures, 14-15 refreshes each, 1 rebuild each. But the evaluator's verified reward increments (actor.py:344-352) are passed into policy.observe_batch (actor.py:414, 423), then agent.observe, then model.observe_outcomes, then OutcomeTracker.realize, which sets spec 'reward' (outcome_spec.py:219). They then enter the Bayes channels (reward_in_beliefs=True default, model.py:823), the archive records and the world-model targets. The actor process also calls evaluator.evaluate_goal for logging (actor.py:467-471).
defects: actor.py:414, 423: evaluator-derived reward reaches the actor's beliefs and the learner's training reward (violates meta-reward 2.4 channel separation)
actor.py:467-471: private evaluator queries inside the actor process

Replace evaluate_goal logging with label-spool counts.
Add inference-client mode (cuda=False, no model).

Leakage test: plant a sentinel verified utility (e.g. 7.123456e5) in the operator; assert it never appears in any inference request payload, record observation, record extra or DecisionTrace (scan the spool bytes).

components.name: Versioned learning records + label channel (meta-reward 13.1, CD-01)
components.evidence: Records today carry model_version, extra['state_version'], extra['behavior'] = {policy, logp_kind, selection, n_candidates} (model.py:1414-1424), extra['value'] and extra['lp_prev']. They carry no reward-model, evaluator or environment version, no outcome timestamp separate from t_sim, no proposal distribution with selection probabilities on the distributed path (planner off), and no reward_mode. Intrinsic reward is not recomputed (cam_learner.py:317).
defects: CD-01 NOT_STARTED; stale intrinsic reward trained silently
actions: EventRecord.extra['versions'] = {'schema':'cam-event/4', 'policy':model_version, 'state':state_version, 'fast':fast_version, 'reward_model':psi_version or None, 'credit':{'return':xi_v, 'hindsight':h_v} or None, 'env':sha1(crucible commit + family-set version + reward_mode), 'inference':server_id}. The env hash is opaque and must not reveal the family to the actor.

EventRecord.extra['behavior'] = {'intent_logp', 'proposals':[{'id','logp_proposal','score','value_pred'}], 'selection':'sample|softmax(T)|argmax', 'selection_logp', 'behavior_logp' (joint log-probability of the executed action under the acting distribution: intent + generation + selection), 'temperature', 'deterministic'}. This lets planner and evaluation-gate decisions be trained off-policy instead of being skipped (cam_learner.py:324).

extra['reward_mode']; EventRecord.reward must be 0.0 unless legacy baseline; extra['t_observed'] on post-action records; extra['signals_raw'] = the theta-independent ExperienceSignals parts (costs, elapsed fraction, exact observed values).

New LabelRecord in the interfaces module: label_id, env_id, actor_id, episode_id, goal_id, status, utility, value, t_resolved_days, t_released_wall, evaluator_version (verifier name + code hash), protocol_hash, split ('train'|'validation'|'heldout'), meta. 'heldout' labels go to an eval root outside run_dir that LearnerSpec never receives.

Recomputation rule: the learner always recomputes R_psi (and the learning-progress part) at update time. A cached actor-side value is used only if psi_version matches and the theta lag is at most the validated L; otherwise, if recomputation is impossible, the decision is dropped from L_policy with reason 'stale_intrinsic'. Per update, log {'psi_version', 'reward_recomputed', 'reward_cached_used', 'evaluator_versions', 'labels_used', 'label_lag_days'}.

Tests: psi bump between act and train gives the recomputed reward; label utilities never appear in actor or inference payloads; the learner process cannot open the heldout root; a label record with an unknown evaluator_version is excluded from predictor training.

components.name: Toy mechanism proofs (toyworld, lagsweep, interference)
components.evidence: test_one_actors_experience_changes_another_actors_behaviour passes in the non-GPU suite (toy GRU, real multiprocess, with an lr=0 control). Toy throughput 1931/5942/9470/11025 decisions/s actors-only and 1692/1872/1809 end to end (bench_toy.json). These numbers do not transfer: CAM is about 0.4 decisions/s per actor, roughly 4 orders of magnitude slower.
defects: Valid only for the toy; must not be cited as CAM evidence (F03 and F04 limitations already say so)
actions: Keep as regression tests; extend lagsweep with a CAM mode (see the off-policy component).

requirements.justification: With real CAM (TINY core 1.92M + Qwen3-0.6B) on real ow_tiny worlds, one central update trained only on actor0's 6 decisions changed actor1's later actions at 6 of 6 steps (5 of 6 tools differ), while the v0 determinism control was identical. In a real 4-process run, actors 1-3 acted under v1..v15 trained only on actor0. It is not EMPIRICALLY_DEMONSTRATED as shared learning: reward is 0, the policy gradient share is about 1e-5, and the change comes from world-model gradients. There is no measure of improvement.

The queue carried real CAM records in multi-process runs (416 events, 0 dup, 0 quarantine). WAL/SIGKILL/consumer-crash tests pass. The label channel and record versions (CD-01) are still missing but belong to separate requirements.

Atomic publication and decision-boundary refresh work (17 publishes, all actors refreshed v0..v15). The latent rebuild covers Z only, not FastState. CAM validation is structural only. Measured at 1.2B params: 30-55 s per publish, 15 s per fetch, 35 GB RSS, so this needs a redesign for the DOM scale.

Per-decision lag tracking and PPO-fresh/V-trace-stale routing are correct in the CAM path (mp4b: 6 PPO, 90 V-trace, rho mean 0.73, ESS 0.84). But CAM runs default to the toy's validated max lag 32 (no lag_validation_cam.json), and the actor-side intrinsic learning-progress reward is trained stale.

CAM has been measured only at 1 actor (0.24 decisions/s) and 4 actors (1.60 decisions/s total, learner 0.45 trained decisions/s, so the learner is the bottleneck at about 3.5x). There are no 8/16-actor CAM runs and no CAM retention or interference measurements; those exist for the toy only. Per-process model copies prevent scaling at the DOM size.
Accounting merges processes correctly (gpu_s, cpu_s, tokens, peak memory in mp4b). There are no dev/main/superlearner CAM throughput benchmarks, and gpu_s is a span, not busy time.
No reward-model, evaluator or environment version fields; no proposal distribution or selection probability on the distributed path; intrinsic reward is not recomputed (cam_learner.py:317).
For the distributed learner: weights-only restart; optimiser state, psi, curriculum state, pending labels and sampler cursors are not persisted (learner.py:403-411).
The distributed CAM learner trains on the evaluator's take_rewards increments (actor.py:344-352, cam_learner.py:318), and the env is Crucible 4.0 without reward_mode. No R_psi is used in dist.

Full OpenWorld learning with 1B core + Qwen3-4B cannot run in the current distributed design: about 14 GB per actor process for the model copy, and publication/fetch takes tens of seconds per version. It is blocked on the central batched inference server and the in-memory weight propagation.

distributed.risks:
1. GPU budget. On the single shared 48 GB A6000, the superlearner scale (32x1536, about 1.0-1.2B core) plus Qwen3-4B fits only if the learner and inference share one process and one frozen Qwen copy (about 36 GB projected). Separate actor processes with model copies are impossible beyond 2-3. Other auditors and jobs on the card reduce the headroom further, so main-scale runs need the card to themselves.

2. Throughput. CAM today runs at 0.4 decisions/s per actor and the learner at 1.65 s per trained decision at TINY scale. At the DOM scale, without batching, an 8-day OpenWorld lifetime (hundreds to thousands of decisions) would take hours per actor. Batched decoding across sessions is the main lever. Learner cost per decision will grow roughly 50-100x with 1B core + 4B decoder cross-attention gradients, so updates must be micro-batched and replay-amortised.

3. Exactness. The current lag-0 'exact' recomputation relies on B=1 math-SDPA kernels. Batched inference will break the bitwise match. The design must rely on importance ratios with a deviation diagnostic, not on exactness.

4. Staleness. Decision-boundary refresh with about 10 s updates made 93% of trained decisions off-policy (ESS about 0.84 at lag 1-2 now, 0.34 in smoke). A 1B policy that changes about 11% of its parameters per step could make V-trace weights collapse, so the CAM lag must be validated.

5. No learning signal. In observation_only mode the current distributed learner has no reward at all until R_psi is integrated, and the world-loss scale dominates the backbone gradient. Without both fixes, 'shared learning' stays world-model learning.

6. Channel integrity. Today evaluator rewards flow into actor beliefs. Moving to envs/experience.py must also remove reward_in_beliefs and the evaluate_goal logging, with sentinel leakage tests, or reward-integrity claims will fail.

7. Disk and durability. Storing per-decision Z_prev at superlearner scale costs about 0.8 TB per 1M decisions (221 GB free). The rental ends 2026-11-30 03:00 UTC, so durable training checkpoints (optimiser, psi, labels) need an off-box destination.

8. Concurrent edits. The repository HEAD moved during this audit (new commits 24274eb..223a589: experience adapter, intrinsic reward, 1B scale). None of them touch dist/, but line numbers outside dist/ (model.py, config.py) may shift.
