learning.summary: The real stack trains end to end on real Crucible MechWorld experience: frozen Qwen3-0.6B, dev scale, 59.8M trainable CAM parameters, of which 14.5M are core. Only four or five losses ever run: world, adapt, actor, value, and memory at HEAD. The keys meta, imagined, retention, action and semantic are never produced. The policy objective is not the tested ActorCriticObjective but an ad-hoc copy, agent.objective_policy. It applies PPO ratios to lag-1 'survivor' rows: 464 of 471 logged real updates, with |ratio-1| above the clip range in 184. It takes one gradient step per batch and needs an environment-supplied reward, so it cannot run in observation-only mode. In the shared core the world-model loss swamps decision learning. Measured on the real stack: world takes 96.1% of the backbone gradient at update 1 and 99.6% at update 4. The actor takes 0.95% and then 0.25%. At update 4 world/actor is about 4400x at block 0 and about 290x at block 7. Every update is clipped (pre-clip norm 115-5883 against a clip of 1.0). The per-objective probe is computed but dropped from logs by experiments/train.py, so 0 of 471 updates logged it. V-trace and GAE are mathematically correct: they match a direct float64 hand computation to 1.8e-15 in both learn/returns.py and dist/offpolicy.py. "Learned exploration" in the integrated agent is a fixed coefficient (lp_coef=0.1) times a one-step, uncorrected hindsight learning progress (LP) added to the env reward, plus a BUDGET token. A trainable experiment-choosing component exists only as the test-double GRU. In the integrated A09 experiment, 7 of 7 runs (LP or extrinsic, lp_coef 0.1 or 1.0, entropy 0.003 or 0.05) collapse to always-safe: return 3.0 against a Bayes-optimal 10.0, with mean LP credited to run_test about 1.7e-4 nats. A09 is therefore FAILED_EMPIRICALLY. J_meta (MetaRLObjective) only reweights rewards and then runs PPO (RL^2 style). It has no differentiable parameter-level inner update and is not called anywhere in the runtime. The same holds for TrialRunner, SupportQueryLoss, the hindsight LP in explore.py, imagined_actor_critic and LearningProgressCurriculum. The integrated adapt loss (model.adapt_loss) scores queries from latent states that have already absorbed earlier query observations. The curriculum has no held-out leakage path, but it is not integrated: training draws families uniformly through TaskStream. Bottom line: keep the math pieces (returns, ActorCriticObjective, Trajectory, ValueHead, BudgetEncoder, SupportQueryLoss, the trainer's mechanics). Replace the learning loop itself (agent.update/objective_policy plus experiments/train.py) with one integrated algorithm: an intrinsic reward R_psi drives functional inner updates of a small fast-parameter set; the outer objective is verified query outcomes (Zheng et al. 2020); loss balancing is on by default and gradients are logged per group. Nothing in the current trainer can host psi or an inner/outer split. The only meta-gradient code is the tabular reference credit/meta_exact.py (commit e7f454b), which the master committed concurrently during this audit; it is not wired into the runtime.

components.name: learn/meta.py (SupportQueryLoss, belief_callables_from_modules, MetaRLObjective/J_meta, TrialRunner) and the integrated model.adapt_loss
components.evidence: grep: MetaRLObjective, TrialRunner, SupportQueryLoss and belief_callables_from_modules are referenced only in learn/ and tests/cam_unified/learn (with learn_doubles). MetaRLObjective.shaped_reward (meta.py:448-455) only reweights rewards (trial/support weights, cost, +lp_coef*intrinsic) and then runs ActorCriticObjective: RL^2-style. It has no inner parameter update and no gradient through adaptation (manifest D07 limitation). The integrated adapt objective is model.adapt_loss (model.py:1677-1731). Support steps update the particle/Kalman belief; query step t is scored from Zs[t] (model.py:1715), which filter_sequence (model.py:1619-1665, ctx with st.obs at 1655) built from every observation up to t, including the outcomes of earlier query steps k..t-1. The belief B_S is support-only but the latent is not, so NLL-vs-k is confounded with one-step-ahead filtering. Real logs: adapt_k is drawn from {0,1,2,4,8,16,32} (k=64 never reachable with adapt_seq_len=33). No torch.func / functional_call / create_graph exists anywhere in learn/ or agent.py. The only meta-gradient code is credit/meta_exact.py (tabular, committed concurrently as e7f454b, unused by the agent).

components.name: Meta-gradient engine (Zheng et al. 2020 intrinsic-reward meta-gradient at CAM scale)
components.evidence: Absent from the audited learner. credit/meta_exact.py:inner_updates_exact/sampled_meta_gradient (tabular, autograd create_graph) and selfeval/intrinsic.py IntrinsicReward/LifetimeValue were added by the master during this audit (commits e7f454b, d975c10) and are not called by agent.py or train.py. Hosting constraints read from the code: policy_evaluate (model.py:1534-1582) recomputes the whole step (tokenizer -> core -> reasoner -> option -> ActionGenerator.log_prob) and deep-copies registries. Weight-dependent caches keyed on model.weights_epoch (model.py:827-884, outcome_spec.py:290-329) serve only under no_grad. The tool-choice parameters are ActionGenerator.tool_q/tool_k/tool_prior and ev_* (semantic/actions.py:135-144); options are OptionModule (1.35M); the BUDGET token is BudgetEncoder (0.19M).
defects: (missing) no functional fast-weight path, no psi optimiser, no outer verified-query objective, no lifetime value in the learner - important
actions: Create learn/metagrad.py. FastPolicy is a functional module over precomputed, detached features from policy_evaluate (R, goal, belief, tool tokens, evidence tokens). Its params are a dict phi for the CAM intent head (DOM-04), the tool pointer (tool_q, tool_k, tool_prior), the typed argument heads, OptionModule, the intrinsic critic V_int, optionally rank-8 LoRA adapters on the top 2 core blocks and the DOM-05 cross-attn gates. The target total is <= 50M params. The 1B core, Qwen, world model and beliefs are never inner-updated.

Inner step (K=1..3, truncated): phi_{k+1} = phi_k - alpha * grad_phi L_inner(phi_k; psi, D_support), with L_inner = the PPO/V-trace surrogate on stored decisions and rewards r_t = R_psi(features_t). Use torch.func.functional_call(FastPolicy, phi, feats) and torch.autograd.grad(..., create_graph=True).

Outer step: J_outer = mean over query decisions collected AFTER the real inner update of logpi_{phi_K}(a|s) * (U_verified - V_L(s)), with U_verified the verified outcome labels and V_L the lifetime value bootstrap until delayed labels arrive (the LIRPG/Zheng practical scheme). grad_psi by autograd; separate AdamW for psi (selfeval/intrinsic.py meta_parameters()).
Bump model.weights_epoch whenever acting with fast weights, so the no_grad caches cannot serve slow-weight embeddings.

Tests: (1) on a 2-layer d=64 CAM stack, the meta-gradient wrt psi at K=1 agrees in direction with central finite differences of the same deterministic surrogate J_outer (cosine > 0.99, float64); (2) detach_inner=True gives exactly zero grad_psi; (3) grad of the actor loss wrt psi is None or zero; (4) a peak-memory test on the 1B core with K=2 stays under 40 GB; (5) EX-J: on capabilities ProbeEnv H=3, 3 seeds, the meta-trained R_psi makes the real agent test first with p > 0.8 and reach a return >= 8.0 of 10, while on the uninformative variant the test rate stays <= 0.1.

actions: Keep explore.py's math (gaussian_decomposition, categorical_decomposition, noise_corrected_lp, hindsight_learning_progress) as feature extractors for ExperienceSignals/R_psi (selfeval/intrinsic.py), never as the reward itself.

requirements.justification: Shown only with the test GRU (learn_doubles.ProbeAgent) and an exact ArmBelief. Through the integrated agent (capabilities/exploration.py, wave-2 Y), 7/7 runs (LP 0.1 / 1.0, extrinsic, entropy 0.003 / 0.05) converge to always-safe: return 3.0 against a Bayes-optimal 10.0, p_test_first 0.000, LP credited to run_test about 1.7e-4 nats. LP and extrinsic are indistinguishable. Exploration credit is a fixed scalar lp_coef on a one-step LP, not a trainable exploration objective.

explore.py hindsight LP with support/query disjointness and the epistemic correction is correct at unit level (tests pass). It is not integrated: the runtime uses model.py:1497-1500, a one-step uncorrected LP, which is ineffective (A09). Meta-exploration over full trajectories exists only in MetaRLObjective, which is unused in the runtime.
The baselines (math_assist / diagnostics) exist and their tests pass, but the 'learned' rows are the GRU test double on the probe bandit only. No comparison with the real CAM agent exists.
OptionModule is integrated in acting and gets actor gradient (1.27 at update 4 on the real stack). option_targets / the SMDP option critic are not used by the integrated policy objective.

ActorCriticObjective (PPO fresh / V-trace stale) is correct; V-trace matches the hand definition to 1.8e-15. The integrated agent does not use it: agent.objective_policy applies PPO ratios to lag-1 rows in 464/471 real updates (|ratio-1| > clip in 184; ratio_maxdev up to 30.9), with one step per batch and env-supplied rewards.

SupportQueryLoss (unit) is correct but unused. The integrated model.adapt_loss restricts only the belief to the support; queries are scored from Zs[t], which absorbed earlier query observations (model.py:1715 with filter_sequence 1655). k=64 is unreachable at adapt_seq_len=33.
J_meta is reward reweighting plus PPO (meta.py:448-470), with no differentiable inner adaptation or meta-gradient, and it is never called by the runtime (grep).

The trainer runs in the real stack (stage continual, three groups, bf16, clipping, exact per-objective core norms, which I reproduced: world share 0.961 at update 1, 0.996 at update 4). Real training never logged the probe (dropped by train.py _scalars, 0/471). World-loss dominance is unmitigated, against spec 12.5. Stages 1/5/6/7 objectives are never produced.

The LP curriculum with diversity floor works in simulation (243/78/79 draws to learnable/noise/mastered). It is not integrated (TaskStream is uniform). The guard is an exact-string denylist unless allowed is given. No held-out leakage path was found in the real stream (worldgen.SplitGuard).
No functional / truncated differentiable inner update exists in learn/ or agent.py. Only the tabular reference credit/meta_exact.py (committed concurrently) exists.
No outer verified-query objective, psi optimiser or lifetime-value bootstrap in the learner.

Measured on the real dev stack (update 4): actor reaches core blocks 0/4/7 (0.0068 / 0.105 / 0.106), tokenizer, beliefs, world_model, reasoner, option and BUDGET. Value reaches the core (0.014 late). action_generator.bridge and the semantic group get 0 from every objective. There is no intent head, R_psi, latent cross-attn or exploration policy to verify. No automated per-group gradient test or log exists.
No loss/parameter/gradient-routing table; one AdamW over everything; no role separation.

learning.risks: 1) Second-order meta-gradients through the 1B core will not fit on one 48 GB A6000. The engine must restrict inner updates to a functional fast set of 50M parameters or fewer, over detached features, with truncated K<=3. Anything larger needs first-order or implicit approximations, and finite-difference checks must then show the truncation bias. 2) Observation-only mode removes the only signal the current actor has. Until R_psi and the verified-label channel exist, the actor learns nothing; R_psi bootstrapping needs LP/VOI features and lifetime-value baselines from day one. 3) World-loss dominance (96-99.99% of core gradient) means any decision-side redesign will appear to fail unless balancing and gradient boundaries come first. Measure shares before judging the new algorithm. 4) Delayed verified outcomes make the outer objective high-variance and lagged. Lifetime value V_L and RUDDER/COCOA credit must be trained on verified outcomes only, or psi will be meta-trained against its own predictions (reward hacking). Keep the reward-integrity tests: planted evaluator-private sentinels, and the gradient of the actor loss wrt psi equal to 0. 5) Fast weights plus no_grad caches keyed on weights_epoch can silently serve stale embeddings; bump the epoch on every fast-weight change. 6) Every positive learned-exploration claim so far rests on doubles with exact Bayesian beliefs. The learned belief is miscalibrated (LP on play_safe -0.73 nats, 'belief misspecification persists' warnings in my runs), so LP-style features may be noise until the belief and world-model subsystems are fixed. 7) Other agents committed new code (credit/, selfeval/) on this branch during the audit, so the HEAD audited for learn/ is 70c2b22 plus later commits that do not touch learn/, agent.py or experiments/. 8) I measured at dev scale (core 14.5M) and over short horizons (<= 4 updates per probe run). Gradient shares and PPO staleness numbers at main/1B scale may differ and must be re-measured with the named-group probe.
